conditions.summary: Decommissioning and site reinstatement within 30 years 6 months or 6 months after cessation
conditions.text:
Within 6 months of the cessation of energy generation from the site, or a period of 30 years and 6 months following commencement of construction, whichever is the sooner, all infrastructure associated with the solar farm (above and below ground) will be removed from the site and the former agricultural use reinstated.
Reason: The land should be reinstated to facilitate future beneficial use in accordance with Policy CC/2 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Removal of development within 6 months of solar farm ceasing to be operational
conditions.text:
All development must be removed from site within 6 months of the solar farm ceasing to be operational.
Reason: The application site lies in the open countryside and it is important that once the development has ceased the site is brought back into a rural use in accordance with the provisions of the NPPF and Policy CC/2 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Hard and soft landscaping carried out in accordance with approved details
conditions.text:
All hard and soft landscape works and boundary treatment shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. The works shall be carried out prior to the operation of the development or in accordance with a programme agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. If within a period of five years from the date of the planting, or replacement planting, any tree or plant is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies, another tree or plant of the same species and size as that originally planted shall be planted at the same place, unless the Local Planning Authority gives its written consent to any variation.
Reason: To ensure the development is satisfactorily assimilated into the area and enhances biodiversity in accordance with Policies HQ/1 and NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Badger protection details to be followed (approved under S/4028/19/CONDA)
conditions.text:
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the badger protection details approved under application S/4028/19/CONDA.
Reason: To minimise disturbance, harm or potential impact upon protected species in accordance with Policy NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018 and their protection under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

conditions.summary: No removal of vegetation or structures during bird nesting season (1 Mar – 31 Aug) without survey
conditions.text:
No works to or removal of hedgerows, trees or shrubs, brambles, ivy and other climbing plants if appropriate, or works to or demolition of buildings or structures that may be used by breeding birds shall take place between 1st March and the 31st August inclusive, unless a competent ecologist has undertaken a careful, detailed check of vegetation for active birds' nests immediately before the vegetation is cleared and provided written confirmation that no birds will be harmed and/or that there are appropriate measures in place to protect nesting bird interest on site. Any such written confirmation should be submitted to the local planning authority.
Reason: To minimise disturbance, harm or potential impact upon protected species in accordance with Policy NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018 and their protection under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity enhancement details to be followed (approved under S/4028/19/CONDA)
conditions.text:
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the biodiversity enhancement details approved under application S/4028/19/CONDA.
Reason: To enhance ecological interests in accordance with Policy NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage to be carried out in accordance with approved details (S/4028/19/CONDA)
conditions.text:
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the surface water drainage details approved under application S/4028/19/CONDA.
Reason: To ensure that the proposed development can be adequately drained and to ensure that there is no increased flood risk on or off site resulting from the proposed development in accordance with Policies CC/8 and CC/9 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage maintenance in accordance with approved details (S/4028/19/CONDA)
conditions.text:
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the surface water drainage maintenance details approved under application S/4028/19/CONDA.
Reason: To ensure the satisfactory maintenance of drainage systems that are not publicly adopted, in accordance with the requirements of Policies CC/8 and CC/9 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018 and the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination – remediation strategy to be submitted if found
conditions.text:
If during the development contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site, such as putrescible waste, visual or physical evidence of contamination of fuels/oils, backfill or asbestos containing materials, then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority) shall be carried out until the developer has submitted, and obtained written approval from the Local Planning Authority for, a remediation strategy detailing how this unsuspected contamination shall be dealt with. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, property and ecological systems, and to ensure that the development can be carried out safely without unacceptable risks to workers, neighbours and other offsite receptors in accordance with Policies CC/7 and SC/11 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: No external lighting without prior approved scheme
conditions.text:
No external lighting shall be provided or installed within the site other than in accordance with a scheme which has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the operation of the development. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To minimise the effects of light pollution on the surrounding area in accordance with Policy NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Retention of historic doors locked in situ; covering details to be approved

Where the overlaying or other means of covering the door is agreed, details of the proposed works shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority prior to installation. The works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: To avoid harm to the special interest of the listed building (Cambridge Local Plan 2018, policy 61).

conditions.summary: Recording and storage of historic doors removed for fire regulations

Reason: To avoid harm to the special interest of the listed building (Cambridge Local Plan 2018, policy 61).

conditions.text:

Reason: Approval of the proposal on a permanent basis would be contrary to Policy CC/2 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018 and the land should be reinstated to facilitate future beneficial use.

conditions.summary: Removal of all development within 6 months of cessation of operation
conditions.text:

Reason: The application site lies in the open countryside and it is important that once the development has ceased the site is brought back into a full agricultural use in accordance with the provisions of the NPPF and Policy CC/2 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved landscaping details (drawing L.0298_13-N)
conditions.text:
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved landscaping details shown on drawing L.0298_13-N (Site Layout and Planting Proposals).
Reason: To ensure the development is satisfactorily assimilated into the area and enhances biodiversity in accordance with Policies HQ/1 and NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with Biodiversity Management Plan (updated 2025)
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the Biodiversity Management Plan F2 dated 15 September 2015 by Avian Ecology (as amended by Biodiversity Management Plan received 2 December 2025 ref 251114 MBL_BMP_2015 (2025 UPDATE)).
Reason: To achieve biodiversity enhancement on the site in accordance with adopted Policies S/3, HQ/1 and NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Calculations
conditions.text:
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the Flood Risk Assessment dated December 2014 by PFA Consulting and Revised Drainage Calculations dated January 2016 by PFA Consulting unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To prevent the increased risk of flooding in accordance with Policies S/3 and CC/9 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with Written Scheme of Investigation for Archaeology

Reason: To secure the provision of archaeological excavation and the subsequent recording of the remains in accordance with Policy NH/15 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

Reason: To minimise the effects of light pollution on the surrounding area in accordance with Policy SC/9 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Restriction of use to specified Use Classes only
conditions.text:
The units, hereby approved, shall be limited to use classes falling within retail (Class E(a)), sale of food and drink (Class E(b)), industrial processes (Class E(g(iii))) and non-institutional education (Class F1(a)) and shall be used for no other purpose (including any other purposes in Class E of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 or in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking or re-enacting that Order with or without modification).
Reason: The application has been assessed on its individual merits and the use of the premises for any other purpose may result in harm which would require re-examination of its impact in accordance with Policy HQ/1 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: No amalgamation of individual units beyond approved drawings
conditions.text:
The individual units, hereby approved, with the exception of units 2, 3 and 4 shall not be amalgamated into larger sized units than is indicated within these approved drawings reference PPS22-3858-ULP1 Rev E without expressed planning consent from the local planning authority.
Reason: To ensure that the use remains small scale in keeping with its rural location in accordance with policies E/17 and E/23 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Restriction of goods sold to food supply statement; no convenience goods
conditions.text:
Unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority, the type of goods sold by the retail units hereby permitted shall be limited to those outlined within the Elsworth food supply statement submitted (received 20th March 2023). No convenience goods shall be sold within these units hereby permitted.
Reason: To ensure that the type of goods sold are compatible with the rural location in accordance with Policy E/23 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Pedestrian footway link from site entrance to existing footway network
conditions.text:
No later than the April 2026, evidence of the outcome of the Cambridgeshire County Council's Local Highway Improvements initiative (comprising of a pedestrian footway link between the site access and the existing footway network) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority. If the outcome of this initiative has been unsuccessful, no later than May 2026, details of a pedestrian footway link, 2-metres width where possible, from the application site's entrance to the existing footway fronting No.29 Brockley Road in addition to a pedestrian dropped kerb to facilitate pedestrians crossing Brockley Road shall be submitted to and agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. The footway and dropped kerb shall be installed in accordance with the approved plans and shall be installed no later than March 2027 whether funded under the Local Highway Improvements initiative or whether funded by the applicant.
Reason: To promote sustainable transport methods and ensure satisfactory pedestrian access to the site in accordance with Policy TI/2 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Ecological measures in accordance with Preliminary Ecological Appraisal
conditions.text:
All ecological measures and/or works shall be carried out in accordance with the details contained in the Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (Skilled Ecology, March 2023) as already submitted with the planning application and agreed in principle with the local planning authority prior to determination.
Reason: To conserve and enhance ecological interests in accordance with Policies HQ/1 and NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain Plan to be submitted within 3 months
conditions.text:
Within 3 months of the date of this decision notice, a Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The BNG Plan shall target how a net gain in biodiversity will be achieved through a combination of on-site and / or off-site mitigation. The BNG Plan shall include: i) A hierarchical approach to BNG focussing first on maximising on-site BNG, second delivering off-site BNG at a site(s) of strategic biodiversity importance, and third delivering off-site BNG locally to the application site; ii) Full details of the respective on and off-site BNG requirements and proposals resulting from the loss of habitats on the development site utilising the latest appropriate DEFRA metric; iii) Identification of the existing habitats and their condition on-site and within receptor site(s); iv) Habitat enhancement and creation proposals on the application site and /or receptor site(s) utilising the latest appropriate DEFRA metric; v) An implementation, management and monitoring plan (including identified responsible bodies) for a period of 30 years for on and off-site proposals as appropriate. The BNG Plan shall be implemented in full and subsequently managed and monitored in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To provide ecological enhancements in accordance with the NPPF 2021 para 174, South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018 policy NH/4 and the Greater Cambridge Shared Planning Biodiversity SPD 2022.

conditions.summary: Ecology enhancement scheme (bat/bird boxes, hedgehog connectivity) within 3 months
conditions.text:
Within 3 months of the date of this decision notice, a scheme of ecology enhancement shall be supplied to the local planning authority for its written approval. The scheme must include details of bat and bird box installation, hedgehog connectivity, and other enhancements as applicable and in line with the Greater Cambridge Biodiversity Supplementary Planning Document (2022). The approved scheme shall be fully implemented within an agreed timescale unless otherwise agreed in writing.
Reason: To conserve and enhance ecological interests in accordance with Policies HQ/1 and NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be approved prior to installation
conditions.text:
No new external lighting shall be provided or installed other than in accordance with a scheme which has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall be carried as approved and shall be retained as such.
Reason: To minimise the effects of light pollution on the surrounding area and to protect biodiversity interests in accordance with Policies SC/9 and NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Details of secure cycle parking for 21 cycles to be submitted within 3 months
conditions.text:
Within 3 months the date of of this decision notice, details of facilities for the secure parking of 21 cycles for use in connection with the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the type and layout. The facilities shall be provided within 6 months of the development hereby approved and in accordance with the approved details and shall be retained as such.
Reason: To ensure appropriate provision for the secure storage of bicycles in accordance with Policy TI/3 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Electric vehicle charge points installed and operational within 3 months
conditions.text:
The electric vehicle charge points and associated infrastructure as detailed in and as shown on drawing PPS22-3858-ULP1 Rev E shall be fully installed and operational within 3 months of this decision notice unless otherwise agreed in writing with the local planning authority.
Reason: In the interests of encouraging more sustainable modes and forms of transport in accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF 2021) paragraphs 107, 112, 174 and 186, policy TI/3 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan and the Greater Cambridge Sustainable Design and Construction SPD 2021.

conditions.summary: Opening hours of units and café use including special events
conditions.text:
The opening hours of the units hereby permitted shall take place only between the hours of 09:00-18:00 each day Monday to Wednesday, 09:00-21:30 Thursday to Saturday and 10:00-16:00 on Sundays, Bank Holidays and Public Holidays. The café use only (Unit 2/3/4) shall operate between the hours of 08:00-18:00 Monday to Wednesday, 08:00-21:30 Thursday to Saturday and 10:00-16:00 on Sundays, Bank Holidays and Public Holidays with the exception of special events (up to 12 per calendar year) where said event shall only take place between the hours of 08:00-22:00 on any day.
Reason: To safeguard the residential amenity of neighbouring occupiers in accordance with Policy HQ/1 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Delivery hours restricted to 07:00-19:00 Mon-Sat and 07:00-17:00 on Sundays/Bank Holidays
conditions.text:
Deliveries to the site shall take place only between the hours of 07:00-19:00 Monday to Saturday and 07:00-17:00 on Sundays, Bank Holidays and Public Holidays.
Reason: To safeguard the residential amenity of neighbouring occupiers in accordance with Policy HQ/1 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: No external amplified music, voice or sound without express planning consent
conditions.text:
There shall be no external playing of any amplified music, voice or sound outside the units, hereby approved, without expressed planning consent from the local planning authority.
Reason: To safeguard the residential amenity of neighbouring occupiers in accordance with Policy HQ/1 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Soft landscaping scheme to be submitted within 3 months and implemented
conditions.text:
Within 3 months of the date of this decision notice, details of a soft landscaping scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These details shall include: planting plans; written specifications (including cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment); schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers/densities where appropriate and an implementation programme. If within a period of five years from the date of the planting, or replacement planting, any tree or plant is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies, another tree or plant of the same species and size as that originally planted shall be planted at the same place as soon as is reasonably practicable, unless the Local Planning Authority gives its written consent to any variation. All soft landscape works shall be carried out and maintained in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure the development is satisfactorily assimilated into the area and enhances biodiversity in accordance with Policies HQ/1 and NH/4 of the South Cambridgeshire Local Plan 2018.

conditions.summary: Conditions 1–11 and 13–15 of parent permission 25/01378/S73 to continue to apply
conditions.text:
Conditions 1-11 and 13-15 of planning permission 25/01378/S73 shall continue to apply to this permission. Where the replicated conditions pertaining to 25/01378/S73 have been discharged, the development of this permission shall be carried out in accordance with the terms of discharge and those conditions shall be deemed to be discharged for this permission also unless alternative details are otherwise agreed through a separate discharge of the conditions as set out above.
Reason: To define the terms of the application.

conditions.text:

Reason: In the interests of good planning, for the avoidance of doubt and to facilitate any future application to the Local Planning Authority under Section 73 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

conditions.summary: Management plan to be submitted within 7 days of use commencing
conditions.text:
Within 7 days of the use hereby permitted commencing, a management plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The management plan shall include provisions relating to: a) the day-to-day management of the property (including staffing levels of security and support staff) and how any anti-social issues will be addressed. b) the external display of contact information for on-site management issues and emergencies for members of the public. c) details of guidance for tenants re acceptable standards of behaviour/use of the premises d) details on how the external spaces will be used and managed throughout the day and evening e) a report after a year of management and a review mechanism of the operation of the approved management plan. f) ongoing engagement with local residents and exploration of the formation of a community liaison group g) how the management plan has reflected consultation with the Council's Housing and Homelessness Department, the Anti-social Behaviour Team and Cambridgeshire Constabulary h) and any other matters pertinent to the management of the premises. The development shall be managed in accordance with and upon discharge of the approved plan. In the interim period before the written approval of the management plan, the use shall be managed in accordance with the Carter Jonas Cover Letter dated 25.07.2025, Crossways House Conditions of Stay and Winter Provision for Rough Sleepers Licence Agreement.
Reason: In order to ensure the occupation of the site is well managed and does not give rise to significant amenity issues for nearby residents (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 policies 35 and 47).

conditions.summary: Covered secure cycle parking details to be submitted within 28 days
conditions.text:
Within 28 days from the date of this decision, details of facilities for the covered, secure parking of cycles for use in connection with the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the means of enclosure, materials, type and layout of the cycle store. A cycle store proposed with a flat / mono-pitch roof shall include plans providing for a green roof. Any green roof shall be planted / seeded with a predominant mix of wildflowers which shall contain no more than a maximum of 25% sedum planted on a sub-base being no less than 80 millimetres thick. The cycle store and green roof as appropriate shall be provided and planted in full in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation or commencement of use and shall be retained as such. The cycle storage facilities shall be provided in full within 3 months of the approval of the details.
Reason: To ensure appropriate provision for the secure storage of bicycles, to encourage biodiversity and slow surface water run-off (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 policies 31 and 82).

Reason: In the interests of good planning, for the avoidance of doubt and to facilitate any future application to the Local Planning Authority under Section 73 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

conditions.summary: Pre-commencement traffic management plan for construction
conditions.text:
No demolition or construction works shall commence on site until a traffic management plan has been submitted to and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

The principal areas of concern that should be addressed are:
i) Movement and control of muck away vehicles (all loading and unloading should be undertaken where possible off the adopted public highway)
ii) Contractor parking, with all such parking to be within the curtilage of the site where possible
iii) Movements and control of all deliveries (all loading and unloading should be undertaken off the adopted public highway where possible.)
iv) Control of dust, mud and debris, and the means to prevent mud or debris being deposited onto the adopted public highway.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: To ensure that before development commences, highway safety will be maintained during the course of development. (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 Policy 81).

conditions.summary: Pre-commencement airborne dust mitigation and monitoring scheme
conditions.text:
No development shall commence until a scheme to minimise the spread of airborne dust from the site including subsequent dust monitoring during the period of demolition and construction, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved scheme.

Reason: To protect the amenity of nearby properties (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 policy 36).

conditions.summary: Piling method statement – noise and vibration mitigation (BS 5228)
conditions.text:
In the event of piling, no development shall commence until a method statement detailing the type of piling, mitigation measures and monitoring to protect local residents from noise and/or vibration has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Potential noise and vibration levels at the nearest noise sensitive locations shall assessed in accordance with the provisions of BS 5228-1&2:2009 Code of Practice for noise and vibration control on construction and open sites.

Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved statement.

Reason: To protect the amenity of the adjoining properties. (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 policy 35).

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination – cease works and submit investigation/remediation
conditions.text:
If unexpected contamination is encountered during the development works which has not previously been identified, all works shall cease immediately until the Local Planning Authority has been notified in writing. Thereafter, works shall only restart with the written approval of the Local Planning Authority following the submission and approval of a Phase 2 Intrusive Site Investigation Report and a Phase 3 Remediation Strategy specific to the newly discovered contamination.

The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Intrusive Site Investigation Report and Remediation Strategy.

Reason: To ensure that any unexpected contamination is rendered harmless in the interests of environmental and public safety (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 policy 33).

conditions.summary: Construction and demolition hours restriction
conditions.text:
No construction or demolition work shall be carried out and no plant or power operated machinery operated other than between the following hours: 0800 hours and 1800 hours on Monday to Friday, 0800 hours and 1300 hours on Saturday and at no time on Sundays, Bank or Public Holidays, unless otherwise previously agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: To protect the amenity of the adjoining properties. (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 policy 35).

conditions.summary: Restriction on construction-phase delivery and collection hours
conditions.text:
There should be no collections from or deliveries to the site during the demolition and construction stages outside the hours of 0800 hours and 1800 hours on Monday to Friday, 0800 hours to 1300 hours on Saturday and at no time on Sundays, Bank or Public Holidays unless otherwise previously agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: To protect the amenity of the adjoining properties. (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 policy 35).

conditions.summary: Flood risk mitigation measures to be implemented prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the occupation of any part of the development, the mitigation and protection measures, as set out in the Flood Risk Assessment at the Varsity Hotel by Simpon Consulting Engineers dated August 2025 (ref. P21-715_V1.0A) shall be fully carried out and shall be retained as such thereafter.

Reason: To prevent the increased risk of flooding (Cambridge Local Plan 2018, policy 32).

Demolition or construction vehicles with a gross weight in excess of 3.5 tonnes shall service the site only between the hours of 09.30hrs -15.30hrs, seven days a week.

Reason: To ensure that before development commences, highway safety will be maintained during the course of development. (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 Policy 81).

conditions.text:

The principal areas of concern that should be addressed are: i) Movement and control of muck away vehicles (all loading and unloading should be undertaken where possible off the adopted public highway) ii) Contractor parking, with all such parking to be within the curtilage of the site where possible iii) Movements and control of all deliveries (all loading and unloading should be undertaken off the adopted public highway where possible.) iv) Control of dust, mud and debris, and the means to prevent mud or debris being deposited onto the adopted public highway. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Intrusive Site Investigation Report and Remediation Strategy.

Reason: To ensure that any unexpected contamination is rendered harmless in the interests of environmental and public safety (Cambridge Local Plan 2018 Policy 33).

conditions.summary: Refusal: Inappropriate Green Belt development – no very special circumstances
conditions.text: The proposed development is not considered to comply with any exception set out at paragraphs 154 or 155 of the NPPF 2024, and therefore is considered to be inappropriate development in the Green Belt. The benefits of the development including the provision of housing, including 50% affordable housing, compliance with the Golden Rules set out at paragraphs 156 and 157 of the NPPF, provision of land for a care home, provision of land for a neighbourhood centre and associated economic benefits, flood risk betterment, and provision of open space, sports pitches and associated community building, are not considered to clearly outweigh the harms arising. The harms identified include definitional harm to the Green Belt, harm to Green Belt openness, conflict with Green Belt purpose (a), landscape harm, failure of the Flood Risk Sequential Test, and the loss of Best and Most Versatile agricultural land. As such, there are no very special circumstances that would justify the grant of planning permission as set out at paragraph 143 of the NPPF. The scheme would fail to comply with the NPPF (2024), Policy SADM26 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan (2016) and Policy CS13 of the Core Strategy (2013). Accordingly planning permission is refused.

conditions.summary: Refusal – inappropriate Green Belt development, no Very Special Circumstances
conditions.text: The proposal is not considered to comply with any exception within Paragraph 154 or 155 of the NPPF 2024, and therefore is considered inappropriate development in the Green Belt. The benefits identified including the provision of housing, medical centre land and primary school land is not considered to outweigh the harm to the Green Belt and landscape harm identified. The proposal would therefore not provide Very Special Circumstances in accordance with Paragraph 143 of the NPPF (2024) and therefore the development is refused. The scheme would fail to comply with the NPPF (2024), SADM26 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Plan and CS13 of the Core Strategy.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination reporting and remediation
conditions.text: In the event contamination is found at any time when carrying out the approved development, it must be reported in writing immediately to the Local Planning Authority. An investigation and risk assessment must be undertaken in accordance with details to be agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. Where remediation is necessary, a remediation scheme must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Following completion of measures identified in the approved remediation scheme a verification report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Hard landscaping scheme to be submitted and approved prior to development above ground
conditions.text: No development above ground level shall take place until details of a hard landscaping scheme for the site have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These details shall include proposed finished levels and contours showing any earthworks and/or mounding; surfacing materials; boundary treatments and means of enclosure; car parking layouts; other vehicle and pedestrian access, circulation / turning areas; hard surfacing materials; minor artefacts and structures (for example outdoor seating areas, cycle storage, refuse/recycling, storage units, and similar features, etc); proposed and existing functional services above and below ground... The scheme shall be implemented prior to the first use of any part of the proposed development.

conditions.summary: Landscape management plan to be submitted and approved prior to development above ground
conditions.text: No development above ground level shall take place until a landscape management plan, including long term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules and periods for all soft landscape areas together with a timetable for the implementation of the landscape management plan, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The landscape management plan shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and timetable.

conditions.summary: Arboricultural Method Statement required prior to commencement
conditions.text: Prior to commencement of development (including any demolition, groundworks and site clearance) in any given phase, an Arboricultural Method Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority relating to that phase. The Statement(s) should include details of the following: a) Tree Protection Plan and measures for the protection of those trees and hedges on the application site that are to be retained; b) Details of all construction measures within the 'Root Protection Area'...; c) A schedule of proposed surgery works to be undertaken to those trees and hedges on the application site which are to be retained. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Method Statement(s) unless agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan to be submitted and approved prior to commencement

Thereafter the construction of the development shall only be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan. The Construction Management Plan/Statement shall include details of: a. Construction vehicle numbers, type, routing; b. Access arrangements to the site; c. Traffic management requirements; d. Construction and storage compounds (including areas designated for car parking, loading / unloading and turning areas); e. Siting and details of wheel washing facilities; f. Cleaning of site entrances, site tracks and the adjacent public highway; g. Timing of construction activities (including delivery times and removal of waste) and to avoid school pick up/drop off times; h. Provision of sufficient on-site parking prior to commencement of construction activities; i. Post construction restoration/reinstatement of the working areas and temporary access to the public highway; j. where works cannot be contained wholly within the site a plan should be submitted showing the site layout on the highway including extent of hoarding, pedestrian routes and remaining road width for vehicle movements; k. Phasing Plan.

conditions.summary: Development to begin within three years of decision notice
conditions.text:
The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning from the date of this decision notice.
Reason: To comply with the provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

conditions.summary: Development to be carried out in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in this notice, other than where those details are altered pursuant to the requirements of the conditions of this planning permission.
Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

conditions.summary: New external work and finishes to match existing adjacent original work
conditions.text:
All new external work and finishes and work of making good shall match the existing adjacent original work in respect of the materials, colour, texture, profile, and finished appearance, except where indicated otherwise on the drawings hereby approved, or unless otherwise required by condition.
Reason: To ensure that the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and that it preserves the character and appearance of the Conservation Area (policies Q2, Q5, Q8, Q11 and Q22 of the Lambeth Local Plan 2021).

conditions.summary: Cycle parking details to be submitted and approved prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the occupation of the development hereby permitted, details of the provision to be made for cycle parking shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The cycle parking shall thereafter be implemented in full in accordance with the approved details before the use hereby permitted commences and shall thereafter be retained solely for its designated use.
Reason: To ensure adequate cycle parking is available on site and to promote sustainable modes of transport (Policies T1, T3 and Q13 of the Lambeth Local Plan 2021).

conditions.summary: Waste and recycling storage details to be submitted and approved prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the occupation of the development hereby permitted, details of waste and recycling storage shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The waste and recycling storage shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to the occupation of the development hereby permitted and shall thereafter be retained solely for its designated use. The path from the refuse stores to the collection point shall be rendered with a smooth finish. The waste and recycling storage areas/facilities should comply with the Lambeth's Refuse & Recycling Storage Design Guide (2022), unless it is demonstrated in the submissions that such provision is inappropriate for this specific development.
Reason: To ensure suitable provision for the occupiers of the development, to encourage the sustainable management of waste and to safeguard the visual amenities of the area (Policies Q2 and Q12 of the Lambeth Local Plan 2021).

conditions.summary: Parking, manoeuvring, loading and unloading scheme to be implemented prior to occupation
conditions.text:
The scheme for parking (including the disabled bay), manoeuvring, and the loading and unloading of vehicles shown on the submitted plans shall be laid out in accordance with the approved details prior to the initial occupation of the development hereby permitted and that area shall not thereafter be used for any other purpose, or obstructed in any way.
Reason: To enable vehicles to draw off, park and turn clear of the highway, minimising danger, obstruction and inconvenience to users of the adjoining highway and to minimise impact on amenity (policies T1, T6, T7 and Q2 of the Lambeth Local Plan 2021).

conditions.summary: Operational plant noise limit not to exceed background level (BS4142:2014)
conditions.text:
Noise from any mechanical equipment or building services plant, as measured in accordance with BS4142: 2014, shall not exceed the background noise level L90B(A) 15 minutes, when measured outside the window of the nearest noise sensitive or residential premises.
Reason: To protect the amenities of adjoining occupiers and the surrounding area (policy Q2 of the Lambeth Local Plan 2021).

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan to be adhered to; site vehicle provision before works commence
conditions.text:
The proposed development hereby approved shall be undertaken in accordance with the submitted Construction Management Plan. No construction works shall commence until provision has been made to accommodate all site operatives', visitors' and construction vehicles loading, offloading, parking and turning within the site or otherwise during the construction period in accordance with the approved details. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the details and measures approved in the Method Management Plan.
Reason: To avoid hazard and obstruction being caused to users of the public highway and to safeguard residential amenity from the start of the construction process (Policy T4 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy T7 of the Lambeth Local Plan 2021).

conditions.summary: Inappropriate development in Green Belt – no very special circumstances
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority considers that the proposed new industrial building constitutes inappropriate development within the Green Belt and it is therefore harmful by definition. The development of an industrial building in addition to the expanse of hard surfacing and additional vehicle parking and movements is not appropriate or compatible with the purposes of the Green Belt and as no very special circumstances have been demonstrated the proposal would be contrary to saved Policy N33 of the adopted Leeds Unitary Development Plan (Review 2006) and guidance given in the National Planning Policy Framework (2023).

conditions.summary: Detrimental to openness of Green Belt – no very special circumstances
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority considers that the proposal of an industrial building in addition to the expanse of hard surfacing and additional vehicle parking and movements, would be detrimental to the openness of the Green Belt. In the absence of very special circumstances, the application is contrary to saved Policy N33 of the Leeds Unitary Development Plan (Review 2006) and guidance given in the National Planning Policy Framework (2023).

conditions.summary: Absence of noise impact assessment – harmful noise to neighbouring residents
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority consider that, in the absence of a noise impact assessment or similar, it is not possible to assess the impact that the proposed activity and vehicle movements could have on neighbouring properties and as such, the proposal could result in unduly harmful levels of noise and disturbance that would reduce the living conditions of the neighbouring residential occupants. The proposal is therefore contrary to saved Leeds UDP (Review 2006) Policy GP5 and the advice set out in the National Planning Policy Framework (2023).

conditions.summary: Inadequate visibility splays and unsafe vehicle movements onto Whitehall Road
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority considers that the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the required visibility splays can be achieved at the access at its junction with Whitehall Road, the acute angle of the access with Whitehall Road, an unenforceable vehicle protocol and a lack of swept path analysis may lead to unsafe vehicle movements onto Whitehall Road, and cause vehicles to wait on Whitehall Road, and as such would occasion danger and inconvenience to users of the highway and be detrimental to highway safety. As a result, the proposal is contrary to advice contained in Policy T2 of the Core Strategy Selective Review 2019 and guidance given in "Manual for Streets" and the Leeds City Council Transport SPD.

conditions.summary: Internal access too narrow for two-way vehicle access – highway safety risk
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority considers that the internal access is too narrow to allow two-way vehicle access and that the site access is not wide enough for vehicles to manoeuvre in and out of the site simultaneously which may lead to vehicles waiting on Whitehall Road leading to a likelihood of accidents and would occasion danger and inconvenience to users of the highway and be detrimental to highway safety. For these reasons, the proposal is considered to be detrimental to highways and pedestrian safety, contrary to Core Strategy Strategic Review Policy T2 and guidance given in "Manual for Streets" and the Leeds City Council Transport SPD.

conditions.summary: Absence of drainage strategy – risk to culverts, rising mains and flood risk
conditions.text: In the absence of a drainage strategy and layouts precisely identifying the location of the culverts and rising water mains that cross the site, the Local Planning Authority consider that proposed development may seriously jeopardise the ability to maintain the culverts and rising main. In the absence of any drainage details or diversion proposals, it is considered that this would increase the flood and water supply risk to surrounding properties. This is contrary to guidance contained within the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Core Strategy Strategic Review (2019) Policy EN5, DPD policies WATER 4 and saved policy GP5 of the Unitary Development Plan (Review) 2006.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above.
For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

conditions.summary: External walling materials – samples to be approved before construction
conditions.text:
Construction of external walls to any building subject of this permission shall not take place until details and samples of all external walling materials have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The walls shall be constructed from the approved materials.
In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Noise management plan prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to occupation, a noise management plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall detail the measures that will be taken to effectively control noise arising at the premises from all likely noise sources so that it does not have an adverse impact on nearby residents. The plan shall include a scheme to deal with noise from:
o Vehicle reversing sounders
o Use of specific loading bays at night-time to minimise impact at dwellings on Farm Hill Road
The approved noise management plan shall be fully implemented before use commences and operated in accordance with the approved plan thereafter.
In the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: BREEAM design stage and final certification prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the occupation of the development design stage certification and final BREEAM certification shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
In the interests of sustainability.

conditions.summary: As-built BRUKL report prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the occupation of the development an as-built BRUKL report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
In the interests of sustainability.

conditions.summary: Solar thermal, PV and ASHP location and capacity details prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the occupation of the development the details of the location and designed capacity of the solar thermal, PVs and ASHP is to be confirmed and shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
In the interests of sustainability.

conditions.summary: Cycle/motorcycle parking to be provided prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Development shall not be occupied until the approved cycle/motorcycle parking and facilities have been provided. The approved facilities shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.
In the interests of highway safety and promoting sustainable travel opportunities.

conditions.summary: Electric Vehicle Charging Points to be provided prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Development shall not be occupied until Electric Vehicle Charging Points have been provided in accordance with a scheme that shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved facilities shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.
In the interest of promoting low carbon transport.

conditions.summary: Replacement planting within 5 years if trees/hedges/shrubs die
conditions.text: If within a period of five years from the date of the planting of any tree/hedge/shrub that tree/hedge/shrub, or any replacement, is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies, or becomes, in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority, seriously damaged or defective, another tree/hedge/shrub of the same species and size as that originally planted shall be planted in the same location as soon as reasonably possible and no later than the first available planting season, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Tree and hedge protection during construction (BS 5837:2012)
conditions.text:
a) No works on any part of the site shall commence until all existing trees, hedges, bushes shown to be retained on the approved plans for that area of the site are fully safeguarded by protective fencing and ground protection in accordance with approved plans and specifications and the provisions of British Standard 5837 (2012) Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Such measures shall be retained for the duration of any demolition and/or approved works.
b) No works or development shall commence on any part of the site until a written arboricultural method statement for a tree care plan for that area of the site has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Works or development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved method statement.
c) No equipment, machinery or materials shall be used, stored or burnt within any protected area. Ground levels within these areas shall not be altered, nor any excavations undertaken including the provision of any underground services, without the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority.
d) Seven days written notice shall be given to the Local Planning Authority that the protection measures are in place prior to demolition and/or approved works, to allow inspection and approval of the works.

conditions.summary: Hydraulic assessment of surface water drainage strategy prior to commencement
conditions.text:
The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved scheme before the development is brought into use, specifically: Development shall not commence until a hydraulic assessment of the proposed surface water drainage strategy has been submitted and approved. Such hydraulic assessment shall use FEH 13 rainfall data set and shall ensure compliance with the following criteria:
(i) For the 50% AEP (1 in 2 year) storm event no pipe surcharge (with exceptions to be agreed)
(ii) For the 3.33% AEP (1 in 30 year) storm event no surface flooding
(iii) For the 1% AEP (1 in 100 year) storm event plus 30% climate change allowance no property flooding with any floodwater retained within the extent of the site
To ensure sustainable drainage and flood prevention in accordance with NTWLP policy Water 7 and GP5 of the UDP.

conditions.summary: CCTV/security system details to be approved before installation
conditions.text:
No CCTV or other security system shall be installed on any unit until full details of proposals have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Details shall include the location and height of any column or supporting structure, position of cameras, field of view and management of surveillance. All equipment shall then be installed in accordance with approved details and retained as such thereafter.
In the interests of visual and residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Full hard and soft landscaping details to be submitted and approved prior to occupation
conditions.text: Notwithstanding the details on the approved plans, the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until full details of both hard and soft landscape works, including a dated implementation programme (inclusive of any phasing), have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Hard landscape works shall include: (a) proposed finished levels and/or contours, (b) boundary details, means of enclosure and retaining structures, (c) car parking layouts including the location and specification of electric vehicle charging points, (d) other vehicle and pedestrian access and circulation areas, (e) hard surfacing areas, (f) minor artefacts, structures and external lighting including measures for bat and bird boxes/infrastructure. Soft landscape works shall include: (g) details of tree and hedge planting, (h) planting plans, (i) written specifications, (j) schedules of plants, (k) drainage proposals, (l) details as to how biodiversity net gain will be achieved in accordance with Core Strategy policy G9.

conditions.summary: Window condition survey and repair/replacement details required prior to installation
conditions.text: Prior to the installation of any new window, a window condition survey, including supporting photographs, shall be submitted to the local planning authority. Where windows are proposed to be repaired the following details shall be provided: - a methodology for the repair of each window to be undertaken by a suitably qualified historic window specialist. Where windows are proposed to be replaced the following details shall be provided: - a justification for why windows have to be replaced rather than are being capable of being repaired, - cross sections with glazing details and profile information, - confirmation of materials and proposed finish, - opening pattern, - Set back location within the window reveal. The windows shall thereafter be repaired or replaced in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Full specification details of new doors to be approved prior to installation
conditions.text: Prior to the installation of any new door, full specification details of the new door, including details of materials and finish, shall be submitted to, and agreed in writing by, the local planning authority. The new doors shall thereafter be installed in accordance with the agreed details.

conditions.summary: Details of external stonework cleaning works to be approved prior to commencement
conditions.text: Prior to any cleaning of external stonework, full details of the cleaning works to be undertaken, including justification for the works from a suitably qualified heritage professional, shall be submitted to, and agreed in writing by, the local planning authority. The cleaning shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the agreed details.

conditions.summary: Details of new stonework including mortar mix to be approved prior to erection
conditions.text: Prior to the erection of any new stonework, full details of the new stonework including mortar mix and joining materials to be used (including a sample panel to be erected on site where requested by the local planning authority) shall be submitted to, and agreed in writing by, the local planning authority. The stonework shall thereafter be erected in accordance with the agreed details.

conditions.summary: Details of new external materials including rainwater goods to be approved prior to addition
conditions.text: Prior to the addition of any new external materials, including rainwater goods or protuberances, full details of the external materials shall be submitted to, and agreed in writing by, the local planning authority. The works shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the agreed details.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above.
For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

conditions.summary: Construction Traffic Management Plan (incl. M1 Motorway consultation)
Statement of Construction Practice (dust, mud, dirt control)
Coal mining intrusive investigations and remediation before above-ground works
conditions.text:
No above ground development shall commence until;
a) a scheme of intrusive investigations has been carried out on site to establish the risks posed to the development by coal mining activity, including that posed by past shallow and opencast coal mining activity, and
b) any remediation works and/or mitigation measures to address land instability arising from coal mining legacy, as may be necessary, have been implemented on site in full in order to ensure that the site is made safe and stable for the development proposed.
The intrusive site investigations and remedial works shall be carried out in accordance with authoritative UK guidance.

conditions.summary: Signed declaration of site safety/stability re coal mining prior to occupation
conditions.text: Prior to the occupation of the development, or it being taken into beneficial use, a signed statement or declaration prepared by a suitably competent person confirming that the site is, or has been made, safe and stable for the approved development shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This document shall confirm the methods and findings of the intrusive site investigations and the completion of any remedial works and/or mitigation necessary to address the risks posed by past coal mining activity.

conditions.summary: Tree and vegetation protection during construction (BS5837)
conditions.text:
a) No works shall commence (including any site clearance, groundworks or drainage etc.) until all existing trees, hedges and vegetation shown to be retained on submitted Drwg. No. DR-6837-01 Rev F (Landscape Masterplan) are fully safeguarded by protective fencing and ground protection in accordance with approved plans and specifications and the provisions of British Standard 5837 (2012) Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Such measures shall be retained for the full duration of any demolition and/or approved works.
b) No works or development shall commence until an updated written Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) in accordance with BS5837 for a tree care plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Works shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved method statement...

conditions.summary: Programme of archaeological recording prior to development
conditions.text:
No development to take place until the applicant, or their agents or successors in title, has secured the implementation of a programme of archaeological recording. This recording must be carried out by an appropriately qualified and experienced archaeological organisation or consultant, in accordance with a written scheme of investigation which has been submitted by the applicant and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
To ensure appropriate level of archaeological observation and recording can take place to prevent irreparable harm being caused to interests of archaeological importance.

conditions.summary: Method Statement for control/eradication of Himalayan Balsam and Giant Hogweed
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of development, including ground works and site preparations, a Method Statement for the control and eradication of Himalayan Balsam and Giant Hogweed (hereafter referred to as the Target Species) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Method Statement will include post-treatment monitoring of the site to ensure a continuous 12-month period of time occurs where none of the Target Species is identified growing on the whole site, if any Target Species is identified as growing on-site during the 12-month monitoring period then treatment shall resume and continue until a continuous 12-month period with no Target Species occurs. The agreed Method Statement shall thereafter be implemented in full.

conditions.summary: Lighting Design Strategy for Bats prior to above-ground development
conditions.text:
Prior to commencement of above ground development a Lighting Design Strategy For Bats shall be produced by an appropriately qualified ecological consultant and submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Strategy shall:
a) Identify those areas/features on site that are particularly sensitive for roosting, commuting or foraging bats- using an appropriately scaled map to show where these areas are
b) Show how and where external lighting will be installed (through the provision of appropriate lighting contour plans and technical specifications) so that it can be clearly demonstrated that areas to be lit will not disturb commuting and foraging bats
All external lighting shall be installed in accordance with the specifications and locations set out in the Strategy, and shall be maintained thereafter in accordance with the Strategy.

conditions.summary: Site access off Aire Valley Avenue details approved prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the occupation of the development details of works comprising the site access off Aire Valley Avenue, as indicated in Drwg. No. 020672-RPS-SI-XX-DR-A-0094 Rev P06 Unit 6- Proposed Site Plan, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved works shall be fully implemented prior to occupation.
To ensure the free and safe use of the highway and to provide adequate pedestrian crossing facilities.

conditions.summary: Electric Vehicle Charging Points provided prior to first use
conditions.text:
The development shall not be brought into use until the Electric Vehicle Charging Points and cable enabled parking spaces for this unit, as indicated in Drwg. No. 020672-RPS-SI-XX-DR-A-0094 Rev P06 Unit 6- Proposed Site Plan, have been provided in accordance with the standards set out in the Council's Transport SPD. The facilities shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.
In the interests of promoting sustainable travel opportunities.

conditions.summary: Cycle parking facilities provided prior to first use
conditions.text:
The development shall not be brought into use until the approved cycle parking facilities associated with the unit's operation have been provided. The approved facilities shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.
In the interests of highway safety and promoting sustainable travel opportunities.

conditions.summary: Vehicular and pedestrian access gradients not to exceed specified limits
conditions.text:
The vehicular access gradient shall not exceed 1 in 40 (2.5%) for the first 15m and 1 in 20 (5%) thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The gradient of the pedestrian access shall not exceed 1 in 20 (5%).
To ensure the free and safe use of the highway, and in the interests of disabled access.

conditions.summary: Existing and proposed ground levels and finished floor levels approved before commencement

applications.applicant: Trustees Of Patrizia Hanover Property Unit Trust

conditions.summary: Insufficient exploration of sustainable transport links to adjacent settlements
conditions.text: The proposed development is located in a designated Rural Area of the Settlement hierarchy in line with the Development Plan's Spatial Development Strategy. Consequently, the proposal lacks sufficient exploration of opportunities to exploit the improvement of sustainable transport links between the development site and adjacent settlements in conflict with the requirements of Core Strategy Policy T1 or National Planning Policy Framework Paragraphs 89 and 114(a). This conflict diminishes the significant weight attributed to the proposal's economic benefits under National Planning Policy Framework Paragraph 85 and prevents the principle of development otherwise being accepted by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Failure to assess significance of non-designated heritage asset and total loss of asset
conditions.text: The proposed development is on a site identified as a non-designated heritage asset (NDHA) by the Local Planning Authority - in line with Historic England Guidance and Annex 2 of the National Planning Policy Framework - and, in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority, the development directly impacts the non-designated heritage asset. The applicant has not described the significance of the affected heritage asset in any level of detail while, at the same time, proposing to remove all physical characteristics of the asset. The applicant is also in possession of a significant level of information pertinent to the significance of the heritage asset that has not been disclosed to the Local Planning Authority. In balancing a judgement on the scheme, the Local Planning Authority consider that the scale of harm amounts to total loss of the asset's significance with no mitigation offered in the form of partial conservation or enhancement. In the absence of an assessment of significance for the heritage asset, in combination with the extent of proposed harm, the application is contrary to the requirements of Core Strategy Policy P11 and National Planning Policy Framework Paragraphs 200 and 209.

conditions.summary: Harm to Leeds Habitat Network with no mitigation or compensation considered
conditions.text: The development site is a constituent part of the Leeds Habitat Network designated by Core Strategy Policy G9 which accords with National Planning Policy Framework Paragraph 185(a). It is the opinion of the Local Planning Authority that the proposal would fully degrade and harm the LHN however the supporting information lacks consideration of the LHN and the impact the development would have - whether this be to the LHN in isolation or the adjacent LWS more widely - while, also not having due regard to potential alternative locations to avoid harm nor considering on-site solutions to mitigate harm or provide an off-site solution to compensate for biodiversity harm contrary to National Planning Policy Framework Paragraph 186 (a) and Core Strategy Policy G8.

conditions.summary: Incomplete bat survey and inadequate protection/mitigation for protected bat species
conditions.text: The development site is identified as having the potential for the roosting, foraging and commuting of various species of bats protected under UK and West Yorkshire BAPs. The application's supporting information provides an incomplete survey of the site alongside contestable conclusions in respect of habitat potential which, in so far as the proposed development seeks to physically remove all existing trees and buildings on the site, has capacity to cause harm to a priority habitat without demonstrating that these concerns are outweighed by need for the development while, at the same time, preventing formation of a methodology to protect, mitigate or compensate for harm to the identified species contrary to Core Strategy Policy G8 and National Planning Policy Framework Paragraph 186 (a).

conditions.summary: Unacceptable highway safety – junction radii, dropped crossings and footway widths
conditions.text: Having regard to the need for all development to be designed to ensure the safety of all highway users, as required by Core Strategy Policy T2 and National Planning Policy Paragraph 114(b) and guided by the Transport and Accessible Leeds SPDs, the proposal fails to fully address highway design matters in relation to vehicular junction radii, pedestrian dropped crossings and footway widths which, cumulatively, are insufficient to protect the safety of pedestrians and those with impaired mobility amounting to unacceptable highway safety concerns, contrary to the guidance contained in the Transport and Accessible Leeds SPDs as well as NPPF Paragraph 114(b) and in line with decision-making practice outlined under NPPF Paragraph 115.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage system fails to demonstrate adequate storage capacity
conditions.text: The proposed surface water drainage system is unable to meet, or at least evidence, minimum operational standards in terms of storage capacity. As such the LPA are not able to confirm that flood risk would not be increased elsewhere contrary to NRWLP Policy Water 4 and National Planning Policy Framework Paragraph 173.

conditions.summary: Failure to demonstrate compliance with District Heating / renewable energy Policy EN4
conditions.text: The development is not able to demonstrate compliance with Policy EN4 in that the proposed development is not supported by appropriate information that addresses either the heat density of the local area or the hierarchy/sequential approach of the District Heating Policy. In the absence of this information the development does not maximise opportunities for carbon savings and renewable energy generation contrary to Policy EN4.
