conditions.summary: Development to commence within three years from 14.08.2024
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from 14.08.2024
Imposed pursuant to the provisions of Sections, 73 and 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above.
For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

conditions.summary: Flood risk and drainage strategy (Mabbett, Project 314936 Rev 3.0)
conditions.text:
The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the Mabbett Flood Risk and Drainage Strategy Project Number 314936 Rev 3.0 dated 26 April 2024, unless otherwise submitted and approved in writing with the Local Planning Authority. The works shall be fully implemented in accordance with the approved scheme before the development is brought into use, or as set out in the approved phasing details.
To ensure as far as reasonably practicable that flood risk is reduced to the property and the users of the property and that appropriate mitigations are in place.

conditions.summary: Car Park and Servicing Management Plan prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Development shall not be occupied until a Car Park and Servicing Management Plan (including timescales) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall include full and finalised details of student pick up and drop off arrangements for the start and end of term. The plan shall be fully implemented, and the development thereafter operated in accordance with the approved timescales.
In the interests of highway safety.

conditions.summary: Revised site layout demonstrating disabled car parking provision
conditions.text:
Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved lower ground floor plan, the parking area shall not be laid out or be brought into use until a revised Proposed Site Layout demonstrating the provision of disabled car parking has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, (in accordance with current British Standard BS8300 unless otherwise agreed in writing). The agreed layout shall be implemented prior to occupation and retained for the lifetime of the development.
To ensure the provision of disabled parking.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved Construction Management Plan and Loading Bay Plan
conditions.text: The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the construction management plan (CPHSP-P=ISSUE 004 FINAL CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT PLAN) date stamped 22.07.2024 and recorded on planning application file 23/07530/FU and Loading Bay Plan (CVH-PL-012 - REV B LOADING BAY) date stamped 19.07.2024 and recorded on planning application file 23/07530/FU. The approved details shall be implemented at the commencement of works on site and shall thereafter be retained and employed until completion of the works on site.

conditions.summary: Electric Vehicle Charging Points scheme prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until full details and a scheme for provision of Electric Vehicle Charging Points, cable enabled spaces and associated infrastructure have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The facilities shall be provided prior to first occupation of the development, retained and maintained thereafter as approved for the lifetime of the development.
In the interest of promoting low carbon transport.

conditions.summary: Cycle/motorcycle parking details prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation, full details of cycle/motorcycle parking and facilities shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved cycle/motorcycle parking and facilities shall be provided prior to first occupation of the development and retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.
In the interests of highway safety and promoting sustainable travel opportunities.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved apartment specification and ventilation drawings (Conservation Area)
conditions.text:
The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the following documentation date stamped as follows and recorded on application file 24/07314/COND: 28 Jan 2025 CVH-GA-005 TYPICAL APARTMENT SPECIFICATION; 28 Jan 2025 CVH-GA-008 VENTILATION PENETRATION; 28 Jan 2025 ACOUSTICS FOR THE MVHR DRAWING; 19 Dec 2024 CVH-GA-007 A ELEVATIONS; 19 Dec 2024 CVH-GA-008 VENTILATION PENETRATION DRAWING.
In the interests of the preservation and enhancement of the Conservation Area, and as approved matters related to the Section 73 permission hereby approved.

conditions.summary: Operational plant noise limit – combined rating level not to exceed background (BS4142:2014+A1:2019)
conditions.text:
The combined noise from any fixed mechanical services and external plant and equipment shall be effectively controlled so that the combined rating level of noise from all such equipment does not exceed the background sound level at any time. Rating level and background sound level are as defined in BS 4142:2014+A1:2019.
In the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved acoustic/MVHR ventilation documents
conditions.text:
The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the following documentation date stamped as follows and recorded on application file 24/07314/COND: 28 Jan 2025 CVH-GA-005 TYPICAL APARTMENT SPECIFICATION; 28 Jan 2025 CVH-GA-008 VENTILATION PENETRATION; 28 Jan 2025 ACOUSTICS FOR THE MVHR DRAWING; 19 Dec 2024 CVH-GA-007 A ELEVATIONS; 19 Dec 2024 CVH-GA-008 VENTILATION PENETRATION DRAWING.
In the interests of residential amenity, and as approved matters related to the Section 73 permission hereby approved.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination – notification, remediation strategy and verification
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately where unexpected significant contamination is encountered during any development works and operations in the affected part of the site shall cease. Where remediation of unexpected significant contamination is considered by the Local Planning Authority to be necessary, a Remediation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the recommencement of development on the affected part of the site. Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion, Verification Report(s) shall be submitted. The site shall not be brought into use until all necessary verification information has been approved in writing.

conditions.summary: Testing and approval of imported soils/soil-forming materials for contamination
conditions.text: Any soil or soil forming materials brought to site for use in garden areas, soft landscaping, public open space or for filling and level raising shall be tested for contamination and suitability for use. A methodology for testing these soils shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to these materials being imported onto site. Testing shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved methodology. Relevant evidence, assessment and verification information shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to the site or phase of the site being brought into use.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved Bat and Bird Plan (31 Jan 2025)
conditions.text:
The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the following documentation date stamped as follows and recorded on application file 24/07314/COND: 31 Jan 2025 BAT AND BIRD PLAN.
In the interests of nature conservation, and as approved matters related to the Section 73 permission hereby approved.

conditions.summary: Integral bat roosting and bird nesting features plan prior to first occupation
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the development, a Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority of: integral bat roosting and integral bird nesting features (for species such as House Sparrow and Swift) within buildings. The agreed Plan shall show the number, specification of the bird nesting and bat roosting features and where they will be located, together with a timetable for implementation and commitment to being installed under the instruction of an appropriately qualified bat consultant. All approved features shall be installed prior to first occupation of the building on which they are located and retained in the manner as approved thereafter.

conditions.summary: Written confirmation of installed bat/bird features with photographs prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to occupation of the building written confirmation of integral bat roosting and/or integral bird nesting features will be submitted to the local planning authority. This should include photographs of features in-situ and a written statement that all features have been installed as per the agreed specifications and locations.
To maintain and enhance biodiversity in accordance with Core Strategy Policy G9, NPPF, and BS 42020:2013.

conditions.summary: Security measures details (lighting, CCTV, access, welfare, etc.) prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation, full details of security measures which include the following items shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority: External lighting; CCTV; Access Controls; Student Management / Welfare plan; Lift Security; Internal and external door and window security measures; Cycle storage security measures. The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved details and retained for the lifetime of the development.
In the interests of resident security, policy H6 of the Core Strategy, Policy GP5 of the saved UDPR.

conditions.summary: Details of roof-mounted energy generation equipment prior to installation (Conservation Area/Listed Buildings)
conditions.text:
Prior to their installation, full location and appearance details of all roof mounted energy generation equipment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall then be undertaken in accordance with the full details.
In the interests of the preservation and enhancement of the Conservation Area and the setting of Listed Buildings.

conditions.summary: Landscaping details and management plan for East Parade elevation lightwell
conditions.text:
Prior to their installation, full details of landscaping treatment including a management plan related to lightwell planting to the East Parade elevation lightwell shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall then be undertaken in accordance with the approved details.
In the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Retention of communal spaces, external amenity space and privacy screening for lifetime of development
conditions.text:
The communal spaces and external amenity space configuration (detailed on all approved floor plans) and the privacy screening to the southern external courtyard (detailed on approved plan CVH-PL-003 rev C) shall be retained in their approved formats for the lifetime of the development.
In the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Removal of external lightwell staircase prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Removal of the external lightwell staircase as detailed on approved plan CVH-PL-003 rev C shall be completed prior to occupation of the proposed development.
In the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Post-construction review statement – energy, carbon and water (within 6 months of completion)
conditions.text:
Within 6 months of completion a post-construction review statement shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority including demonstration that the building(s) have achieved the relevant standards. As part of a post construction review the following evidence is required: An appropriate as-built summary of carbon emission and energy needs must be submitted along with as-built SAP/BRUKL report and EPC for each unit type; As built evidence of water fixtures installed as per the Part G information document published on 26.04.2023.
In the interests of mitigating the effects of climate change.

conditions.summary: 1:20 construction drawings and external materials samples for rear extension prior to commencement
conditions.text:
Prior to the commencement of works to the rear extension full construction standard drawings at a scale of 1:20 details and samples of all external walling and roofing materials shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall then be undertaken in accordance with the approved details.
In the interests of visual amenity and the preservation of the character of the conservation area.

conditions.summary: External walling and roofing materials samples for rear extension prior to commencement
conditions.text:
Prior to the commencement of works to the rear extension full details and samples of all external walling and roofing materials shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Materials shall be made available on site and the Local Planning Authority provided with 7 days written notice of their availability. The development shall then be undertaken in accordance with the approved details.
In the interests of visual amenity and the preservation of the character of the conservation area.

conditions.summary: Operational hours restricted to 07:00–19:00 Monday to Sunday including Bank Holidays
conditions.text:
The use hereby permitted shall be limited to operational hours between 07:00 and 19:00 Monday to Sunday, inclusive of Bank Holidays.

In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Open storage use restricted to specified materials and goods only
conditions.text:
The proposed open storage use permitted shall be limited to the storage of the following materials and goods within the site,
- Tools and machinery
- Vehicles and trailers, including caravans
- Building Materials (including but not limited to aggregates, bricks, tiles, masonry, timber, cladding)
- Pallets (both loaded and unloaded)
- Non-hazardous agricultural materials
- Portakabin/Welfare Units
- Steel Stockholders

In the interest of amenity and noise prevention.

conditions.summary: Storage of scaffolding prohibited on site (significant noise generator)
conditions.text:
The use hereby permitted does not include provision for the storage of scaffolding. Scaffolding shall not be stored anywhere within the site as this is identified as a significant potential noise generator by the LPA.

In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Vehicle areas to be laid out, surfaced and drained prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Development shall not be occupied until all areas shown on the approved plans to be used by vehicles, including roads, footpaths, cycle tracks, loading and servicing areas and vehicle parking space have been fully laid out, surfaced and drained such that loose materials and surface water does not discharge or transfer onto the highway. These areas shall not be used for any other purpose thereafter.

To ensure the free and safe use of the highway.

conditions.summary: Approved noise protection scheme (ref NIA-11530-24-11734 V3) to be implemented prior to occupation
conditions.text:
The approved noise protection scheme, ref: NIA-11530-24-11734 V3 submitted 15.11.2024, shall be implemented in full prior to the occupation of any dwelling and shall be retained thereafter.

In the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Plant and machinery noise limited to existing background level (L90) – BS4142:2014 assessment
conditions.text:
Plant and machinery operated from the site shall limit noise to a level no higher than the existing background noise level (L90) when measured at noise sensitive premises, with the measurements and assessment made in accordance with BS4142:2014. The rating level shall include the addition of any character corrections as appropriate. If the character is unknown at the design stage or cannot be evidenced then a penalty of 5dB should be applied to take into account of potential corrections.

In the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Music, amplified sound and tannoy systems not to be audible at site boundary
conditions.text:
Any music or amplified sound including tannoy systems used shall not be audible from any point on the site boundary.

In the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Wind modelling and mitigation measures prior to above-ground superstructure of each phase
conditions.text: 'Within six months of the commencement of the above-ground superstructure of phase 1 and prior to the commencement of the above-ground superstructure of any subsequent phases - wind modelling of that phase shall be submitted to and approved in in writing by the local planning authority. Full working drawing details and an implementation programme of the necessary wind mitigation measures described in (i) Lisbon Street Leeds, Wind Microclimate Report 1V4, FD Global Limited Report (dated 11 August 2024) and Lisbon Street, Phase 2, Leeds, Wind Microclimate Report, FD Global Limited Report (dated 9 June 2025), as well as any further mitigation measures required to ensure acceptable safety and comfort levels within publicly accessible areas of that phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These further mitigation measures will be assessed through the wind modelling. The approved measures for that phase shall be completed in accordance with the approved details and implementation programme and, for the avoidance of doubt, prior to the first occupation of any building in that phase. The measures shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development, or until they are proven to be no longer necessary as part of future phases of development. In the interests of public safety'

conditions.summary: Restriction on number of residents and staff on site at any one time

conditions.summary: Bin store details to be approved prior to occupation

conditions.summary: Statement of Construction Practice to be submitted and approved prior to commencement
conditions.text: The development shall not commence until a Statement of Construction Practice has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Statement of Construction Practice shall include full details of: a) the means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles and associated traffic management measures; b) methods to prevent mud, grit and dirt being carried on to the public highway; c) measures to control the emissions of dust and dirt during construction; d) details of measures to protect soil to the front of the site; e) hours of operation on site which shall be limited to 0800-1800 Monday to Friday; 0800-1300 on Saturdays, and no working on Sundays or Bank Holidays; and f) how the statement of construction practice will be made publicly available by the developer.

conditions.summary: Tree and vegetation protection measures and Arboricultural Method Statement
conditions.text: a) No works shall commence (including any site clearance, groundworks or drainage etc.) until all existing trees, hedges and vegetation are fully safeguarded by protective fencing and ground protection in accordance with approved plans and specifications and the provisions of British Standard 5837 (2012) Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. b) No works or development shall commence until a written Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) in accordance with BS5837 for a tree care plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. c) Evidence shall be submitted that confirms that a qualified Arboriculturist/competent person has been appointed to carry out arboricultural monitoring/supervision. d) Seven days written notice shall be given to the Local Planning Authority that the protection measures are in place prior to demolition/approved works commencing. e) No equipment, machinery or materials shall be used, stored or burnt within any protected area.

conditions.summary: Detailed drawings of external building works at 1:20 scale prior to commencement
conditions.text:
The following external building works shall not be commenced on the relevant part of the development until drawings showing typical details at a scale of not less than 1 to 20 have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority: (i) Details and sections of any new external windows and reveals, including curtain walling and rooflights; (ii) Details of new heads, cills and string courses; (iii) Details and sections of any new external doors; (iv) Details and sections of any new, rainwater goods and supporting brackets; and (v) Details of any external vents or pipes. The works shall be carried out in accordance with the details thereby approved prior to first occupation of the development. Notwithstanding the submitted drawings all existing external windows other than for those removed as a direct result of the position of the extension shall be retained and refurbished unless justification for their replacement is first agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

In the interests of visual amenity and the special qualities of the listed building.

conditions.summary: Detailed drawings of internal building works at 1:20 scale prior to commencement
conditions.text:
The following internal building works shall not be commenced until typical drawings and sections at a scale of not less than 1:20 and details of the following features have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority: 1. Any proposed fire upgrading requirements to existing doors in the building; 2. Details of new internal doors; 3. Details of the measures to seal the redundant door in the hallway involving retention of the existing door. 4. Details of ventilation systems for bathrooms and kitchens including routes, terminations and vents; and 5. Details of any insulation requirements to walls or floors. The works shall be constructed in accordance with the details thereby agreed prior to first occupation of the development.

In the interests of visual amenity and to protect the special qualities of the listed building.

conditions.summary: Samples of external walling and roofing materials to be approved prior to construction

Samples shall be made available on site prior to the commencement of building works, for inspection by the Local Planning Authority which shall be notified in writing of their availability. The building works shall be constructed from the materials thereby approved.

In the interests of visual amenity.

In the interests of visual amenity and to protect the special qualities of the listed building.

Full working drawing details and an implementation programme of the necessary wind mitigation measures described in (i) Lisbon Street Leeds, Wind Microclimate Report 1V4, FD Global Limited Report (dated 11 August 2024), Lisbon Street, Phase 2, Leeds, Wind Microclimate Report, FD Global Limited Report (dated 9 June 2025) and Lisbon Street, Hotel Phase, Leeds, Wind Microclimate Report, FD Global Limited Report (dated 4th November 2025), as well as any further mitigation measures required to ensure acceptable safety and comfort levels within publicly accessible areas of that phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These further mitigation measures will be assessed through the wind modelling. The approved measures for that phase shall be completed in accordance with the approved details and implementation programme and, for the avoidance of doubt, prior to the first occupation of any building in that phase. The measures shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development, or until they are proven to be no longer necessary as part of future phases of development. conditions.summary: Refusal: Poor residential amenity – over-intensification of HMO use
conditions.text:
The Local Planning Authority considers that the proposed floor layout, lack of separate communal living and dining rooms, under provision of sufficient kitchen floor space and private outside amenity spaces would lead to a poor standard of residential amenity for future occupants through over intensification. This is also demonstrated through harm to:
- Privacy, outlook and reduced light penetration when considering the proximity of the right of way and increased need for curtains/blinds to be closed for bedrooms 01 and 02's privacy
- Poor outlook for the sole windows of bedrooms 04 and 05 facing blank brick walls and curtailed views
- Loss of privacy, poor outlook and reduced light penetration for bedrooms 14, 18 and 25 facing either each other's sole bedroom windows or communal kitchen increasing need for curtains/blinds to be closed for privacy
- Noise and nuisance from the adjacent car park, the entrance hallway/ramp and kitchen uses for bedrooms 07 and 27 with additional loss of privacy/poor light penetration to 07 from closed curtains/blinds
As such, the proposal is considered to be contrary to Policy P10 of the Core Strategy (2019), Policies GP5 and BD5 of the Unitary Development Plan Review (2006), Neighbourhoods for Living SPG, the draft HMO, PBSA and Co-Living Amenity Standards SPD and section 12 of the NPPF.

Development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Phase I Desk Study has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority and:
(a) Where the approved Phase I Desk Study indicates that intrusive investigation is necessary, development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Phase II Site Investigation Report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority;
(b) Where remediation measures are shown to be necessary in the Phase I/Phase II Reports and/or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Remediation Strategy demonstrating how the site will be made suitable for the intended use has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all works and for the provision of Verification Reports.

To ensure that the presence of contamination is identified, risks assessed and proposed remediation works are agreed in order to make the site 'suitable for use' with respect to land contamination.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination – notification and amended Remediation Strategy

The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. An amended or new Remediation Strategy and/or Soil Importation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any further remediation works which shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the revised approved Strategy.

To ensure that any necessary remediation works are identified to make the site 'suitable for use' with respect to land contamination.

conditions.summary: Remediation works to be carried out per approved Strategy; Verification Report required before use

The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

To ensure that the remediation works are fully implemented as agreed and the site has been demonstrated to be 'suitable for use' with respect to land contamination.

conditions.text:

Where remediation measures are shown to be necessary in the Phase II Report and/or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Remediation Strategy demonstrating how the site will be made suitable for the intended use has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all works and for the provision of Verification Reports.

To ensure that the presence of contamination is identified, risks assessed and proposed remediation works are agreed in order to make the site 'suitable for use' with respect to land contamination.

conditions.summary: Notification and revised strategy required if remediation cannot proceed as approved
conditions.text:

An amended or new Remediation Strategy and/or Soil Importation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any further remediation works which shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the revised approved Strategy.

To ensure that any necessary remediation works are identified to make the site 'suitable for use' with respect to land contamination.

conditions.summary: Remediation works to be carried out per approved strategy with verification report submitted

On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

To ensure that the remediation works are fully implemented as agreed and the site has been demonstrated to be 'suitable for use' with respect to land contamination.

conditions.summary: Inappropriate development in Green Belt – no very special circumstances
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority consider that, by virtue of the change of use of the land, the increased intensity of the use of the land and the associated increase in vehicle parking and movements in an otherwise open and highly exposed location, the proposal is harmful to the openness of the Green Belt and would represent an encroachment of development into the countryside. The result of this is that the development also constitutes inappropriate development by virtue of failing to meet any relevant exceptions in national or local Green Belt policy. In accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework, substantial weight must be afforded to this harm. Given that the limited benefits of the scheme would clearly not outweigh the totality of the Green Belt harms and other harms hereby identified, there are no very special circumstances which exist in this instance. Therefore, the proposal is contrary to Saved Unitary Development Plan Review (2006) Policies N33 and GB19, and guidance within the National Planning Policy Framework (as amended) regarding protecting green belt land.

conditions.summary: Highway safety and accessibility – informal parking and increased vehicle movements
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority considers that, by virtue of the intensity of the proposed use, the siting of the pedestrian access gate, and the proposed vehicle parking layout, the development would encourage the use of the adjacent worn grass verge at the junction of Rhodes Lane and the Public Right of Way for informal vehicle parking, rather than the designated parking provision within Clifford Moor Farm. This would result in the further erosion and degradation of this part of the public highway and introduce unacceptable highway safety risks for users of Rhodes Lane, which is a single-track route. In addition, given that the affected verge forms part of Definitive Bridleway CLIFFORD 6 and lies within a cycleway route designated by the Clifford Neighbourhood Plan, the increased vehicle movements and informal parking would adversely affect the accessibility for pedestrians, cyclists and equestrian users, through the loss of available space on the footway and reduced visibility at the point of crossing Rhodes Lane. As such, the development would be harmful to the safety and accessibility of the highway network for all users, contrary to the requirements of Core Strategy (as amended 2019) Policy T2, Saved Unitary Development Plan Review (2006) Policy GB19, and the National Planning Policy Framework (as amended) in respect of promoting sustainable transport.

Reason: To ensure that the landscaping is designed in a manner appropriate to the locality and to enhance the appearance of the development and to comply with policy CS19 of the Core Strategy and policy SP15 of the Site Allocations and Policies DPD.

conditions.summary: Landscaping implementation and replacement within 5 years if failed
conditions.text:
All changes in ground levels, hard landscaping, planting, seeding or turfing shown on the approved landscaping details shall be carried out during the first planting and seeding season (October - March inclusive) following the commencement of the development or in such other phased arrangement as may be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any trees or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years of being planted die are removed or seriously damaged or seriously diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species.
Reason: To ensure that the landscaping is carried out at the appropriate time and is properly maintained and to comply with policy CS19 of the Core Strategy and policy SP15 of the Site Allocations and Policies DPD.

conditions.summary: Development to follow mitigation measures in Updated Ecology Survey (June 2024)
conditions.text:
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the mitigation measures set out in Updated Ecology Survey 3rd June 2024.
Reason: In the interests of the ecology of the site and to comply with policy CS21 of the Core Strategy and policy SP19 of the Site Allocations and Policies DPD.

conditions.summary: Side-facing bedroom window of Unit 1 to be obscure-glazed (Pilkington Level 3+)
conditions.text:
Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 3, Schedule 2, Part 1 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order (England) 2015 (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification), the side facing bedroom window serving Unit 1 on the approved plan shall be glazed in obscure glass to a level equivalent to Pilkington Level 3 or above before the dwelling hereby permitted is first occupied and shall thereafter be permanently retained in this approved form.
Reason: To protect the privacy and amenities of the occupiers of adjoining property and in accordance with Policy SP15 of the Site Allocations and Policies DPD.

conditions.summary: Permitted development rights removed – no enlargement or outbuildings without consent
conditions.text:
Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 3, Schedule 2, Part 1 Classes A-E of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification), no enlargement, improvement or other alteration to the dwelling, and no provision of buildings, enclosures, swimming or other pool, shall be erected or carried out except with prior planning permission.
Reason: In the interests of the character and appearance of the area and surrounding residential amenity and to comply with policy SP15 of the Site Allocations and Policies DPD.

conditions.summary: Flood risk mitigation measures (including doorway protection for plots 4 and 5) before first occupation
conditions.text:
The development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the mitigation measures as set out in the Michael Evans Flood Risk Assessment 14/03/2024 prior to the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved. This shall include doorway flood protection for plots 4 and 5.
Reason: In the interests of flood risk.

conditions.summary: External lighting details to be approved before first occupation
conditions.text:
Before the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved, details of external lighting on the building and within the grounds, shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Development shall be carried out in accordance with these approved details.
Reason: In the interests of residential amenity and to comply with Policy SP15 of the Site Allocations and Policies DPD.

conditions.summary: Access to be widened to 5m before first occupation
conditions.text:
The access shall be widened to 5m as shown on the approved plan GH-24-10A prior to the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved and shall thereafter be retained in accordance with the approved plan.
Reason: In the interests of highway safety in accordance with Policy SP15 in the Adopted Rutland Local Plan Site Allocations & Policies DPD 2014, Design Guidelines for Rutland (SPD), The National Design Guide (2021) and Paragraph 116 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023).

conditions.summary: Car parking and turning provided and retained in perpetuity per approved plan
conditions.text:
Car parking and turning shall be provided in accordance with plan GH-24-10A prior to the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved and shall thereafter be retained in perpetuity and not used for any other purpose other than the parking and turning of vehicles.
Reason: In order to ensure that sufficient car parking and turning remains available on site in the interests of highway safety in accordance with Policy SP15 in the Adopted Rutland Local Plan Site Allocations & Policies DPD 2014, Design Guidelines for Rutland (SPD), The National Design Guide (2021) and Paragraph 116 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023).

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage on access to prevent flow onto public highway
conditions.text:
The existing access and extension thereof must incorporate a method of surface water drainage to ensure that no private surface water can flow on to the public highway prior to the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved and shall thereafter be so maintained.
Reason: In order to ensure that no private surface water flows on to the public highway in the interests of highway safety in accordance with Policy SP15 in the Adopted Rutland Local Plan Site Allocations & Policies DPD 2014, Design Guidelines for Rutland (SPD), The National Design Guide (2021) and Paragraph 116 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023).

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan to be approved before any demolition or development
conditions.text:
No development shall take place, including any demolition work, until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which will include the following:- a) A scheme for monitoring, reporting and control of construction noise and vibration including hours of working and scope for remedial action b) A scheme for the control of dust and scope for remedial action c) Details of a chassis and wheel cleaning system d) Haul routes to the site and hours of delivery e) Measures to ensure that vehicles entering the site can do so immediately upon arrival f) Details to ensure that any parking, waiting, loading/unloading only occurs in the marked out parking bay g) Details of any events likely to require a banksman h) Details of site compounds, storage area and contractor/visitor parking/turning i) Details of the site enclosure and gated site security j) Confirmation that demolition will be carried out in accordance with the ecological assessment k) Details of site notice with contact details and complaints scheme l) Details of any temporary lighting m) A scheme for recycling/disposing of waste n) The erection and maintenance of security hoarding.
Reason: In the interests of residential amenity and highway safety in accordance with Policy SP15 in the Adopted Rutland Local Plan Site Allocations & Policies DPD 2014.

Reason: To ensure that sufficient turning for the largest anticipated commercial vehicles is provided and maintained in the interest of highway safety in accordance with Policy SP15 in the Adopted Rutland Local Plan Site Allocations & Policies DPD 2014, Design Guidelines for Rutland (SPD), The National Design Guide (2021) and Paragraph 116 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Car and cycle parking areas to be provided prior to occupation and retained
conditions.text:

Reason: To ensure that appropriate parking is provided in the interests of highway safety in accordance with Policy SP15 in the Adopted Rutland Local Plan Site Allocations & Policies DPD 2014, Design Guidelines for Rutland (SPD), The National Design Guide (2021) and Paragraph 116 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan (noise, dust, haulage, lighting, ecology, waste etc.) required pre-commencement
conditions.text: No development shall take place, including any demolition work, until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which will include the following:- a. A scheme for monitoring, reporting and control of construction noise and vibration including hours of working and scope for remedial action. b. A scheme for the control of dust and scope for remedial action in the event that dust is identified as an issue or any complaints are received. c. Haul routes to the site from the strategic road network and hours of delivery. d. Measures to ensure that vehicles can access the site immediately upon arrival to ensure there is no park, waiting, loading/unloading or queuing on the public highway. e. Details of site compounds, storage area and contractor/visitor parking/turning. f. Details of the site enclosure or part thereof and gated site security. g. Confirmation that any demolition will be carried out in accordance with the ecological assessment. h. Details of site notice with contact details and a scheme for dealing with complaints. i. Details of any temporary lighting which must not directly light the public highway. j. A scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from the demolition and construction works. k. The erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan.

conditions.summary: 30-year Habitat Monitoring and Management Plan (HMMP) required pre-commencement
conditions.text:
The development shall not commence until a 30 year Habitat Monitoring and Management Plan (HMMP), prepared in accordance with an approved Biodiversity Gain Plan, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved HMMP shall be strictly adhered to and implemented in full for its duration and shall contain the following: a) Description and evaluation of the features to be managed; b) Ecological trends and constraints on site that may influence management; c) Aims, objectives and targets for management - links with local and national species and habitat action plans; d) Description of the management operations necessary to achieving aims and objectives; e) Preparation of a works schedule, including annual works schedule; f) Details and a timetable of the monitoring needed to measure the effectiveness of management; g) Details of the persons responsible for the implementation and monitoring; h) Mechanisms of adaptive management; and i) Details of methodology and frequency of monitoring reports to be submitted to the Local Planning Authority to assess biodiversity gain.
Reason: To enhance biodiversity, and in accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework and paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

conditions.summary: Public Right of Way Operational Safety Plan required prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation or use of the development, a Public Right of Way (PROW) Operational Safety Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include: An assessment of the operational phase risks to users of Public Footpath E227 arising from vehicle and pedestrian movements within the site following completion of the development; Details of the permanent measures to manage pedestrian/vehicle interaction, including routing, surface markings, lining, signage and visibility improvements; Arrangements for the future monitoring, maintenance and upgrading of the measures where required to ensure continued safe operation for the lifetime of the development. The development shall thereafter operate only in accordance with the approved PROW Operational Safety Plan.
Reason: To safeguard the safety and free passage of users of Public Footpath E227, which runs through and adjacent to the development site, and to ensure that operational phase pedestrian/vehicle interactions are managed to an acceptable standard, in accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework and relevant local planning policies.

conditions.summary: Standard advertisement consent conditions
conditions.text:
i. No advertisement is to be displayed without the permission of the owner of the site or any other person with an interest in the site entitled to grant permission.
ii. No advertisement shall be sited or displayed so as to:
a. endanger persons using any highway, railway, waterway, dock, harbour or aerodrome (civil or military);
b. obscure, or hinder the ready interpretation of, any traffic sign, railway signal or aid to navigation by water or air; or
c. hinder the operation of any device used for the purpose of security or surveillance or for measuring the speed of any vehicle.
iii. Any advertisement displayed, and any site used for the display of advertisements, shall be maintained in a condition that does not impair the visual amenity of the site.
iv. Any structure or hoarding erected or used principally for the purpose of displaying advertisements shall be maintained in a condition that does not endanger the public.
v. Where an advertisement is required under these Regulations to be removed, the site shall be left in a condition that does not endanger the public or impair visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Land contamination: site characterisation, remediation scheme, implementation and reporting
conditions.text:
(i) Site Characterisation: No development shall take place until an assessment of the nature and extent of contamination has been submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA. (ii) Submission of Remediation Scheme: No development shall take place until a detailed remediation scheme has been submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA. The scheme must include all works to be undertaken, proposed remediation objectives and criteria, an appraisal of remedial options, and a timetable of works. (iii) Implementation of Approved Remediation Scheme: The remediation scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved timetable. Within 3 months of completion, a validation report must be submitted. (iv) Reporting of Unexpected Contamination: Any contamination found during development not previously identified must be reported in writing within 5 days to the LPA and development halted on the affected part of the site pending assessment and, where necessary, an approved remediation scheme.

Reason: To ensure that any contamination that may be present on site is identified and addressed.

conditions.summary: Refusal: incongruous kiosks harm setting of Grade II listed hotel and historic landscape
conditions.text: The retrospective timber kiosks, by virtue of their design, form and siting, constitute incongruous and unsympathetic additions within the setting of the Grade II listed Normanton Park Hotel. The structures fail to preserve or enhance the significance of the heritage asset and erode the character and appearance of the historic and designated landscape of the Rutland Water area. No public benefits have been demonstrated that would outweigh this identified less than substantial harm. Accordingly, the development is contrary to Sections 12, 15 and 16 of the National Planning Policy Framework; Policies CS19, CS22 and CS24 of the Rutland Core Strategy; Policies SP7, SP15, SP20, SP21, SP23 and SP26 of the Site Allocations and Policies DPD; and the Design Guidelines for Rutland SPD (2022).

conditions.summary: BREEAM Very Good standard compliance
conditions.text:
Prior to commencement of development excluding demolition works, details of the measures to be undertaken to secure compliance with the BREEAM Very Good standard (or equivalent) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The measures set out within the report shall be implemented. Prior to occupation, the relevant certification shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that as built the development has achieved the BREEAM 'Very Good' Standard or an equivalent standard. The measures shall be thereafter maintained.
Reason: In the interest of promoting energy efficiency and sustainable development.

conditions.summary: Construction hours restriction
conditions.text:
No construction work in connection with the development shall take place on any Sunday or Bank or Public Holiday, nor on any other day except between the following times: Monday to Friday 0730 - 1800 hours, Saturdays 0800 - 1300 hours unless in association with an emergency or with the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority
Reason: To protect the amenity of nearby occupiers.

conditions.summary: Operational hours restriction – weekdays, Saturdays, no Sundays/Bank Holidays
conditions.text:
The use of the premises hereby permitted shall be restricted to the hours of 07:00 to 19:00 on weekdays, 07:00 to 12:00 on Saturdays, and shall not take place at any time on Sundays or Public Holidays.
Reason: In the interests of the amenities of the area.

conditions.summary: Operational plant noise rating level (BS 4142) – 5dB below background
conditions.text:
The rating level of noise emitted from the proposed plant and equipment to be installed on the site (determined using the guidance of the current version of BS 4142 for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) shall be as low as reasonably possible. In general, this is expected to be 5dB below the existing measured background noise level LA90, T. In exceptional circumstances, such as areas with a very low background or where assessment penalties total above 5dB the applicant's consultant should contact the Environmental Protection Team to agree a site specific target level.
Reason: To protect the amenity of nearby occupiers.

conditions.summary: Noise Management Plan prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the occupation and operation of the development, a management plan covering the entirety of the operation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The plan shall include but not be limited to hours of delivery, control of noise from plant and machinery and noise from internal and external activities. The site shall be operated in accordance with the approved plan.
Reason: To protect the amenity of nearby occupiers.

conditions.summary: Infiltration of surface water drainage – controlled waters protection
conditions.text:
No infiltration of surface water drainage into the ground is permitted other than with the written consent of the Local Planning Authority. Where infiltration is to be used to manage the surface water from the development hereby permitted, it will only be allowed within those parts of the site where information is submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority that there is no resultant unacceptable risk to controlled waters and/or ground stability. The development shall only then be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution caused by mobilised contaminants in line with the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Detailed SuDS surface water drainage scheme prior to commencement
conditions.text:
Development shall not begin in any phase until a detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme for the site has been submitted to (and approved in writing) by the local planning authority. The detailed drainage scheme shall be based upon the Sustainable Drainage Options Appraisal & Strategy prepared by Oakshire Environmental dated 5th September 2024 and shall demonstrate that the surface water generated by this development (for all rainfall durations and intensities up to and including the climate change adjusted critical 100-year storm) can be accommodated and disposed of within the curtilage of the site without increase to flood risk on or off-site. The drainage scheme shall also demonstrate appropriate operational, maintenance and access requirements for each drainage feature or SuDS component. The drainage scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure the development is served by satisfactory arrangements for the disposal of surface water and to ensure that the development does not exacerbate the risk of on/off site flooding.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage verification report prior to occupation
conditions.text:
No building on any phase (or within an agreed implementation schedule) of the development hereby permitted shall be brought into use until a Verification Report, pertaining to the surface water drainage system and prepared by a suitably competent person, has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The Report shall demonstrate that the drainage system constructed is consistent with that which was approved. The Report shall contain information and evidence (including photographs) of details and locations of inlets, outlets and control structures; landscape plans; full as built drawings; information pertinent to the installation of those items identified on the critical drainage assets drawing; and, the submission of an operation and maintenance manual for the sustainable drainage scheme as constructed.
Reason: To ensure that flood risks from development to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised.

conditions.summary: Piling – groundwater protection via risk assessment
conditions.text:
Piling or any other foundation designs using penetrative methods shall not be permitted other than with the express written consent of the Local Planning Authority, which may be given for those parts of the site where it has been demonstrated by a piling risk assessment that there is no resultant unacceptable risk to groundwater. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution caused by mobilised contaminants in line with paragraph 174 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Land contamination strategy – site investigation and remediation method statement
conditions.text:
No development shall take place until a strategy to deal with the potential risks associated with any contamination of the site has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. This strategy will include the following components: 1. A site investigation scheme, based on the Phase 1 Preliminary Risk Assessment submitted with the Outline application. 2. A remediation method statement (RMS) based on the site investigation results and the detailed risk assessment. This should give full details of the remediation measures required and how they are to be undertaken. The RMS should also include a verification plan. The development shall thereafter be implemented in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution.

conditions.summary: Land contamination verification report prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of the development herein approved a verification report demonstrating the completion of works set out in the approved remediation method statement and the effectiveness of the remediation shall be submitted to, and approved in writing, by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall include results of sampling and monitoring carried out in accordance with the approved verification plan to demonstrate that the site remediation criteria have been met.
Reason: To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to human health or the water environment by demonstrating that the requirements of the approved verification plan have been met and that remediation of the site is complete.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination – further remediation strategy if found
conditions.text:
If, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority) shall be carried out until a remediation strategy detailing how this contamination will be dealt with has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved.
Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by unacceptable levels of water pollution from previously unidentified contamination sources at the development site in line with the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Method and Mitigation Strategy prior to commencement
conditions.text:
Prior to commencement of development a Biodiversity Method and Mitigation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Strategy shall be based on the mitigation and enhancement recommendations in sections 8 and 9 of the Ecological Habitat Survey Report by Hone Ecology (dated 1.4.22). It must demonstrate that any ecological mitigation can be incorporated into the site. It will also outline further surveys required prior to works, to inform the detailed mitigation strategy. Development shall only be carried out in accordance with the approved strategy.
Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to ensure no adverse impact on ecology and to ensure appropriate mitigation and enhancement measures are carried out.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme – Bat Conservation Trust GN8 and ILP GN01/21 compliant
conditions.text:
External lighting shall only be installed in accordance with a detailed scheme of lighting that has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This scheme shall be designed in accordance with the Bat Conservation Trust's 'Guidance Note 8: Bats and Artificial Lighting 08/23' and take note of and refer to the Institute of ILP Guidance Note 01/21 The Reduction Of Obtrusive Light and shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. The scheme shall demonstrate that existing dark corridors will be maintained and that areas to be lit will not adversely impact biodiversity including boundary vegetation, proposed landscaping and bat/bird boxes.
Reason: In the interests of amenity and biodiversity.

conditions.summary: Parking, cycle parking, EV charging points details via reserved matters
conditions.text:
The details submitted pursuant to condition (1) above shall include details of the provision of visibility splays, vehicle manoeuvring, parking including Electric Vehicle Charging Points and permanent retention of secure covered cycle parking facilities. The development shall then be carried out in complete accordance with the approved details with these measures in place prior to the first occupation of the development herein approved. Publicly accessible EV "rapid charge" point (of 22kW or faster) should be provided (where no dedicated off-street parking is provided) and/or per 1000m2 of commercial floor space.
Reason: In the interests of highway safety and active travel.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan (CMP) prior to commencement
conditions.text:
No development, site clearance or preparation shall take place on the site until the details of a Construction Management Plan (CMP) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The CMP shall include: details of the scale, timing and mitigation of all construction related aspects of the development; numbers, frequency, routing and type of vehicles visiting the site (including measures to limit delivery journeys on the SRN during highway peak hours); measures to ensure that HGV loads are adequately secured; travel plan and guided access/egress and parking arrangements for site workers, visitors and deliveries; sheeting of loose loads and wheel washing and other facilities to prevent dust, dirt, detritus etc from entering the public highway. Thereafter the construction of the development shall proceed in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan.
Reason: To ensure that the A249 Trunk Road and M2 continue to be effective parts of the national system of routes for through traffic.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures in place prior to any site works
conditions.text:
No development, site clearance or preparation shall take place on the site until the tree protection measures as set out on drawing number tr-1630-22 TPP within Appendix D of the Arboricultural Survey and Impact Assessment have been implemented on site. The tree protection measures shall thereafter remain in place throughout the duration of the construction activity.
Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to ensure adequate protection and no irreversible harm to trees.

conditions.text: All existing historic features shall be retained in situ, except where indicated otherwise on the approved drawings. Any internal and external repair works and faēade repairs to the listed building shall accord with the Faēade Condition Survey by PAYE approved under ref 21/500608/SUB as amended by Proposed Outline Faēade Dismantle And Rebuild Methodology, Facade Repair Mark-up, Facade Repair Schedule and drawing 20.061-ONA-00-EL-DR-A-1569 (South Elevation - Bay Repair/Rebuild). Reason: To ensure the quality of the development is maintained and to prevent harm to the listed building.

conditions.summary: Broad method statement for fit-out works to protect listed building interest
conditions.text: Following the initial exploratory demolition, preparatory and strip out works, a broad method statement shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority prior to the detailed fit out scheme commencing. It shall set out the approach to the following matters and shall include mitigation measures necessary to demonstrate that the works/installations will not harm the building's special architectural and historic interest: Plumbing including all ground and above level drainage; Ventilation provision; Mechanical & Electrical services for heating and lighting; Fire strategy - measures for prevention, detection, and means of escape; Acoustic attenuation between spaces; Removal of any asbestos; New interior lighting scheme; Any special measures for kitchens and kitchen storage areas. The development shall be carried out in complete accordance with the approved details. Reason: To protect and preserve the appearance and character of the listed building.

conditions.summary: No false or suspended ceilings to ground floor units or Internal Street
conditions.text: There shall be no insertion of false or suspended ceilings to ground floor units 02, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 04 or the Internal Street. Reason: To protect the historic and architectural interest of the Listed Building.

conditions.summary: Fit-out details for Internal Street, ramp, Historic Asset Space, Gym and Lounge
conditions.text: Within 4 months of consent, details of the fit out for the Internal Street, ramp, first floor Historic Asset Space, Residents' Gym and Residents' Lounge shall be submitted for the approval by the Local Planning Authority. The approved works shall be implemented prior to first use and retained thereafter. No carpets shall be installed and the fit out should aim to conserve the industrial character of the listed building. Reason: To protect the historic and architectural interest of the Listed Building.

conditions.summary: Record photographs to HER and heritage interpretation area to be installed
conditions.text: The full set of record photographs of the existing building submitted under 21/500608/SUB shall be made available to Kent County Council's Historic Environment Record within 2 months of this decision. Within 3 months of first use, heritage interpretation area(s) shall be installed in accordance with details that have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure that the heritage benefits associated with archiving the building's history are secured.

conditions.summary: Vehicular access restricted to approved access points onto local road system
conditions.text:
No vehicular access shall be made onto the existing local road system except via the access points to Scocles Road, Barton Hill Drive and Lower Road as indicated on drawing numbers RLA/01/5; 3319/20 AND 3319/26; RLA/01/10; SHEP 506 AND RLA/01/11A; SHEP 502, 503, 504 & 510 respectively.
Reason: In the interests of highway safety.

conditions.summary: Vehicular access to Kingsborough Park and Norwood Manor via approved roundabout only
conditions.text:
Vehicular access to the housing development to the north of Eastchurch Road (described as Kingsborough Park) and the leisure and recreation development to the south and west of Eastchurch Road (described as Norwood Manor) shall not be obtained other than via the roundabout proposals approved on drawing nos. RLA/01/7 & RLA/01/9c.
Reason: In the interests of highway safety and convenience.

conditions.summary: No vehicular access onto local road system except via approved roundabout
conditions.text:
No vehicular access, other than that required to serve the car park to be provided in association with the community woodland, shall be made onto the existing local road system other than via the roundabout hereby permitted in accordance with drawing no RLA/O1/9c.
Reason: In the interests of highway safety.

conditions.summary: Retention of existing agricultural buildings at Norwood Manor for golf course use
conditions.text:
The existing agricultural buildings at Norwood Manor shall be retained for use in association with the golf course hereby permitted.
Reason: In order to protect the setting of Norwood Manor.

conditions.summary: Development to be maintained in accordance with approved comprehensive drainage management scheme
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be maintained in accordance with the comprehensive drainage management scheme(s) approved pursuant to condition 24 of outline planning permission reference SW/95/0102.
Reason: To prevent pollution of the water environment.

conditions.summary: Surface water from parking areas to pass through oil interceptor before discharge
conditions.text:
Prior to being discharged into any watercourse, surface water sewer or soakaway system, all surface water drainage from parking areas and hardstandings shall be passed through an oil interceptor designed and constructed to have a capacity and details compatible with the site being drained. Roof water shall not pass through the interceptor.
Reason: To prevent pollution of the water environment.

conditions.summary: No development to preclude access to parking, loading and unloading areas
conditions.text:
No permanent development whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (as amended) or not, shall be carried out on the land so shown or in such a position as to preclude vehicular access to space reserved for vehicle and cycle parking and the loading and unloading of commercial vehicles. Access to the land shall be provided prior to the occupation of the premises to which it relates, and shall be used for or be available for use for the parking, loading and off-loading of vehicles at all times when the premises are in use.
Reason: The development without the provision of parking, loading and off-loading space, would be detrimental to amenity and likely to lead to inconvenience and danger to road users by virtue of vehicles parked on the public highway.

conditions.summary: No development to preclude vehicular access to car parking or garages
conditions.text:
No permanent development, whether permitted by the Town and Country (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (as amended) or not shall be carried out on such land (other than the erection of a private garage or garages) or in a position as to preclude vehicular access to land for car parking or garages.
Reason: Development without adequate provision for the parking or garaging of cars is likely to lead to car parking inconvenient to other road users and detrimental to amenity.

conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures to be implemented prior to development above slab level
conditions.text:
No development shall take place above slab level until the tree protection measures as set out in the Tree Survey and Arboricultural Impact Assessment reference 23_5837_04-21 version 1.0 (dated 18/05/2023) have been implemented on site. The tree protection measures shall thereafter remain in place throughout the construction phase of the development.
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance and provision for landscaping in accordance with Policy DM14 of Bearing Fruits 2031: The Swale Borough Local Plan 2017.

conditions.summary: Operational plant noise limit (BS4142) – 5dB below background LA90,T
conditions.text:
The rating level of noise emitted from the proposed plant and equipment to be installed on the site (determined using the guidance of the current version of BS 4142 for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) shall be 5dB below the existing measured background noise level LA90, T. The equipment shall be maintained in a condition so that it complies with the levels specified in the approved acoustic report ('Plant Noise Assessment' by RBA Acoustics dated 25 August 2023 (reference 12963.RP01.PNA.0), whenever it is operating. After installation of the approved plant no new plant shall be used without the written consent of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To safeguard conditions of amenity in accordance with Policy DM14 of Bearing Fruits 2031: The Swale Borough Local Plan 2017.

conditions.summary: Ecological enhancement measures to be submitted and implemented within one month
conditions.text:
Within one month of the date of this decision, details shall be submitted of ecological enhancement measures following the recommendations as set out in the Preliminary Ecological Assessment reference BWE-PEA-SCHME12 (dated 4 May 2023) and a timetable for implementation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The ecological enhancement measures shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure the scheme suitably mitigates against its impact in relation to biodiversity, in accordance with the requirements of Policy DM28 of Bearing Fruits 2031: The Swale Borough Local Plan 2017.

conditions.summary: Archaeological watching brief required prior to groundworks
conditions.text: No groundworks of any kind shall commence (including, but not limited to, the digging of trenches for services and/or foundations or the removal of existing structures) until the applicant, or their agents or successors in title, has secured the implementation of a watching brief to be undertaken by an archaeologist approved by the Local Planning Authority so that the excavation is observed and items of interest and finds are recorded. The watching brief shall be in accordance with a written programme and specification which has first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority; Reason: To ensure that features of archaeological interest are properly examined and recorded.

conditions.summary: External materials to match approved plans – Headcorn Conservation Area
conditions.text: The materials used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall be as shown on the approved plans; Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance and that the historic significance of the Headcorn Conservation Area is maintained.

conditions.summary: Windows to be timber painted white; former showroom fenestration dark aluminium; conservation rooflights
conditions.text: All new and replacement windows shall be constructed from timber and painted white, except for the fenestration of the former tile showroom section of the building which shall be dark aluminium. All roof lights shall be of the conservation type; Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance and that the historic significance of the Headcorn Conservation Area is maintained.

conditions.summary: East-facing side elevation windows to be obscure glazed and fixed shut (privacy)
conditions.text: All new and replacement windows fitted at ground and first floor level in the east-facing side elevation of Moat House, both within the additional residential accommodation hereby permitted and within the existing accommodation, shall be obscure glazed to not less than the equivalent of Pilkington Glass Privacy Level 3 and shall be incapable of being opened, and shall subsequently be maintained as such in perpetuity; Reason: To prevent overlooking of Bryher House and to safeguard the privacy of existing and prospective occupiers.

conditions.summary: Development to comply with flood mitigation measures in approved Flood Risk Assessment
conditions.text: The development shall be carried out in complete accordance with the flood mitigation and resilience measures set out in the Flood Risk Assessment by EP Architects received on 24/08/2023; Reason: In the interests of flood resilient development.

conditions.summary: Development to be carried out in accordance with approved plans and documents
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents: Site location plan and drawing numbers 2010.P.01 Rev B and 2010.P.02 Rev C received on 18/08/2023, and the Flood Risk Assessment by EP Architects received on 24/08/2023; Reason: To clarify which plans and documents have been approved.
