conditions.summary: Development to commence within 3 years of permission date
conditions.text:
The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date on which the permission is granted.
Reason: In pursuance of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: 0601 Rev P4, 0602 Rev P2, 0610 Rev P1, 0701 Rev P3, 0702 Rev P3, 1001 Rev P4, 1050 Rev P2, 1321 Rev P5, 2231-21-01 Rev C, 2235-21-10 S5 Rev P03, 2235-21-11 Rev P04 and 2235-21-12 Rev P01.
Reason: In the interests of proper planning and for the avoidance of doubt.

conditions.summary: Archaeological field evaluation, safeguarding, recording and post-excavation reporting
conditions.text:
To assess and mitigate the impacts of development on significant archaeological remains: A) Prior to any development works within the 'Area of Archaeological Interest' as set out on plan 0610 Rev P1, the applicant shall secure and have reported a programme of archaeological field evaluation works, in accordance with a specification and written timetable approved by the LPA. B) Following evaluation, no development shall take place until safeguarding measures and/or further archaeological investigation have been approved. C) Archaeological safeguarding measures shall be carried out in accordance with agreed specification and timetable. D) Within 6 months of completion a Post-Excavation Assessment Report shall be submitted and approved. E) The measures outlined in the Report shall be implemented in full.
Reason: To ensure that features of archaeological interest are properly examined and recorded.

conditions.summary: Detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme required pre-commencement
conditions.text:
Development shall not commence until a detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme for the site has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The detailed drainage scheme shall be based upon the Drainage Strategy prepared by Hydrock dated 02.10.23 and shall demonstrate that the surface water generated by this development (for all rainfall durations and intensities up to and including the climate change adjusted critical 100 year storm) can be accommodated and disposed of without increase to flood risk on or off-site. The drainage scheme shall also demonstrate that silt and pollutants resulting from the site use can be adequately managed and that appropriate operational, maintenance and access requirements for each drainage feature or SuDS component are adequately considered. The drainage scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure the development is served by satisfactory arrangements for the disposal of surface water and to ensure that the development does not exacerbate the risk of on/off site flooding.

conditions.summary: Oil and petrol interceptors/separators scheme required pre-commencement
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall not be commenced until such time as a scheme to install oil and petrol separators has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The scheme shall be implemented as approved. The scheme shall: Be designed and constructed to have a capacity compatible with the area being drained; Be installed prior to the occupation of the development and thereafter maintained for the lifetime of the development; ensure clean roof water and vehicle washdowns and detergents do not pass through the interceptor(s).
Reason: To reduce the risk of pollution to the water environment.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures to be installed pre-commencement and retained during construction
conditions.text:
No development shall commence until the tree protection measures as set out in drawing no. 2235-21-12 Rev P01 and within the Arboricultural Report have been installed. The protection measures shall remain in place for the duration of the construction and no works, storage or other activity shall take place within a protected area unless specifically identified within the Report. The development hereby permitted shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Updated landscape planting and management plan required prior to above slab level works
conditions.text:
No development beyond the construction of foundations or above slab level shall take place until an updated landscape planting plan and a landscape management plan, incorporating full details of both hard and soft landscape works has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The planting plan must demonstrate that a native species hedgerow will be incorporated into the site and the management plan must detail how all the habitats on site will be established and managed. These details shall also include existing trees, shrubs and other features, planting schedules of plants, noting species (which shall be native species and of a type that will encourage wildlife and biodiversity), plant sizes and numbers where appropriate, means of enclosure, hard surfacing materials, and an implementation programme. All hard and soft landscape works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. The works shall be carried out prior to the occupation of any part of the development.
Reason: In the interests of the visual amenities of the area and encouraging wildlife and biodiversity.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage verification report required prior to occupation
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until a Verification Report, pertaining to the surface water drainage system (subject to conditions 4 and 5) and prepared by a suitably competent person, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Report shall demonstrate that the drainage system constructed is consistent with that which was approved. The Report shall contain information and evidence (including photographs) of details and locations of inlets, outlets and control structures; landscape plans; full as built drawings; information pertinent to the installation of those items identified on the critical drainage assets drawing; and, the submission of an operation and maintenance manual for the sustainable drainage scheme as constructed.
Reason: To ensure that flood risks from development to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised.

conditions.summary: Remediation verification report required prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to any part of the permitted development being occupied, a verification report demonstrating the completion of works set out in the approved remediation strategy by Hydrock dated 01/12/23 and the effectiveness of the remediation shall be submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. The report shall include results of sampling and monitoring carried out in accordance with the approved verification plan to demonstrate that the site remediation criteria have been met.
Reason: To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to human health or the water environment by demonstrating that the requirements of the approved verification plan have been met and that remediation of the site is complete.

conditions.summary: Off-site surface water drainage works to be secured and implemented prior to occupation
conditions.text:
Information shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority that demonstrates that off-site surface water drainage works are appropriately secured and protected and subsequently implemented prior to the occupation of the development.
Reason: To ensure the development is served by satisfactory arrangements for the disposal of surface water.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be approved prior to installation (ILP GN 01/21)
conditions.text:
No external lighting shall be installed unless such details have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This scheme shall be in accordance with the Institute of ILP Guidance Note 01/21 The Reduction Of Obtrusive Light (and any subsequent revisions) and shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. Details of operation hours should also be included. The scheme of lighting shall be installed, maintained and operated in accordance with the approved scheme unless the Local Planning Authority gives its written consent to any variation.
Reason: To protect the amenities of the surrounding area.

conditions.summary: External plant details and noise assessment required prior to installation
conditions.text:
No external plant shall be installed at the site until full details of such plant together with an updated noise assessment that takes into account the specific noise levels of the plant has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The external plant shall be installed, maintained and operated in accordance with the approved scheme unless the Local Planning Authority gives its written consent to any variation.
Reason: To protect the amenities of the surrounding area.

conditions.summary: Building to be constructed to BREEAM 'Good' standard with certification on first use
conditions.text:
The building hereby approved shall be constructed to BREEAM 'Good' Standard, or an agreed equivalent standard, and prior to the first use of the building the relevant certification shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority confirming that the required standard has been achieved.
Reason: In the interest of promoting energy efficiency and sustainable development.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination – remediation strategy required before further development
conditions.text:
If, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority) shall be carried out until a remediation strategy detailing how this contamination will be dealt with has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved.
Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution from previously unidentified contamination sources at the development site.

conditions.summary: Piling restricted unless piling risk assessment demonstrates no groundwater risk
conditions.text:
Piling or any other foundation designs using penetrative methods shall not be permitted other than with the express written consent of the Local Planning Authority, which may be given for those parts of the site where it has been demonstrated by a piling risk assessment that there is no resultant unacceptable risk to groundwater. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution caused by mobilised contaminants.

conditions.summary: Construction hours restricted to 0800-1800 Mon-Fri, 0800-1300 Sat, no Sundays or Bank Holidays
conditions.text:
No demolition/construction activities shall take place, other than between 0800 to 1800 hours (Monday to Friday) and 0800 to 1300 hours (Saturday) with no working activities on Sunday or Bank Holiday.
Reason: In the interest of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: External finishing materials as per approved drawing 1321 Rev P5
conditions.text:
The new building hereby approved shall be constructed using the external finishing materials set out on drawing no. 1321 Rev P5.
Reason: In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Replacement of failed landscaping within 5 years of planting
conditions.text:
Upon completion of the approved landscaping scheme, any trees or shrubs that are removed, dying, being severely damaged or becoming seriously diseased within five years of planting shall be replaced with trees or shrubs of such size and species as may be agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority, and within whatever planting season is agreed.
Reason: In the interests of the visual amenities of the area and encouraging wildlife and biodiversity.

conditions.summary: Electric vehicle charging points to be provided prior to first use and retained permanently
conditions.text:
Prior to the first use of the development hereby permitted, the electric vehicle charging points shown on approved drawing 0601 Rev P4 shall be provided and shall be retained permanently.
Reason: To ensure the provision and retention of electric vehicle charging facilities in the interest of reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

conditions.summary: Car and cycle parking areas to be kept available at all times
conditions.text:
The area shown on approved drawings 0601 Rev P4 and 0701 Rev P3 as car parking space and cycle parking space shall be kept available for such use at all times and no permanent development, whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) or not, shall be carried out on the land so shown or in such a position as to preclude vehicular access thereto; such land and access thereto shall be provided prior to the operation of the light industrial unit hereby permitted.
Reason: Development without adequate provision for the parking of cars is likely to lead to car parking inconvenient to other road users.

conditions.summary: Use restricted to Class E(g)(iii), B2 and B8 only
conditions.text:
The building shall be used in an industrial and/or storage use as defined by Class E (g)(iii), B2 and B8 and for no other purpose whatsoever, including any other purposes in Class E of The Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2020 (as amended) and any other use whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) or not.
Reason: In the interests of protecting the amenity of the surrounding area.

conditions.summary: Materials to match approved plans and application form
conditions.text:
The materials to be used in the development hereby approved shall be as indicated on the approved plans and application form.
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Pre-commencement archaeological field evaluation and investigation
conditions.text:
Prior to the commencement of development hereby approved the applicant, or their agents or successors in title, will secure:
i. archaeological field evaluation works in accordance with a specification and written timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority; and
ii. further archaeological investigation, recording and reporting, determined by the results of the evaluation, in accordance with a specification and timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority;
iii. programme of post excavation assessment and publication.
The development shall only proceed in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure that features of archaeological interest are properly examined, recorded, reported and disseminated.

conditions.summary: Ecology enhancement scheme (swift bricks, bat tubes, wildflower planting etc.)
conditions.text:
The development hereby approved shall not commence above slab level until details of a scheme for the enhancement of ecology on the site have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall consist of the enhancement of ecology through at least one integrated method into the design and appearance of the buildings by means such as swift bricks, bat tubes or bee bricks, and through the provision within the site curtilage such as bird boxes, bat boxes, bug hotels, log piles, wildflower planting and hedgehog corridors. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation of the buildings and all features shall be maintained thereafter.
Reason: To enhance the ecology and biodiversity on the site in the future.

conditions.summary: Contamination discovery protocol and closure report
conditions.text:
If during construction/demolition works evidence of potential contamination is encountered, works shall cease and the site fully assessed to enable an appropriate remediation plan to be developed. Works shall not re-commence until an appropriate remediation scheme has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority and the remediation has been completed. Upon completion of the building works, this condition shall not be discharged until a closure report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The closure report shall include details of: a) Details of any sampling and remediation works conducted and quality assurance certificates; b) Details of any post-remedial sampling and analysis; c) If no contamination has been discovered, evidence to show that no contamination was discovered.
Reason: In the interests of protecting the health of future occupants from any below ground pollutants.

conditions.summary: Construction hours restricted to 0800–1800 Mon–Fri and 0800–1300 Saturday
conditions.text:
No construction activities shall take place, other than between 0800 to 1800 hours (Monday to Friday) and 0800 to 1300 hours (Saturday) with no working activities on Sunday or Bank Holiday. [see informative].
Reason: In the interests of neighbour amenity.

conditions.summary: Plant noise rating level 5dB below background LA90,T (BS 4142:2014)
conditions.text:
The rating level of noise emitted from the proposed plant and equipment to be installed on the site (determined using the guidance of BS 4142 : 2014 Rating for industrial noise affecting mixed residential and Industrial areas) shall be 5dB below the existing measured background noise level LA90, T.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be approved in accordance with ILE GN01:2011
conditions.text:
Any external lighting installed on the site (whether permanent or temporary) shall be in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted details shall be in accordance with the Institute of Lighting Engineers Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Lighting, GN01, dated 2011 (and any subsequent revisions), and shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the subsequently approved details and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the countryside and in the interests of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Operational hours 0730–1800 Mon–Fri and 0800–1300 Saturday; no Sundays or bank holidays
conditions.text:
All activity in connection with the commercial use of the application site and building (including deliveries and despatches) shall only take place between 0730-1800hrs Mon-Fri and 0800-1300 hrs on Saturdays with no activity on Sundays or bank holidays.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: BREEAM 'Very Good' Post-Construction Review Certificate required before occupation
conditions.text:
No part of the development hereby approved shall be used or occupied until a Post-Construction Review Certificate issued by the Building Research Establishment or other equivalent assessors confirming that the development has achieved a BREEAM rating of not less than the standards equivalent to 'Very Good' has been submitted to and acknowledged in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure that the development achieves a high standard of sustainability and makes efficient use of resources.

conditions.text:
The approved buildings shall only be used for warehouse purposes within planning use class B8 (Storage and Distribution).
Reason: The use of the buildings has only been considered in connection with the proposed use and other uses have the potential to result in amenity or highway impacts.

The scheme shall consist of the enhancement of biodiversity through the provision within the site curtilage such as bird boxes, bat boxes, bug hotels, log piles, wildflower planting and hedgehog corridors. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to first commencement of the approved use and all features shall be maintained thereafter.

conditions.summary: Landscaping scheme to be approved and in place prior to use commencement
conditions.text:
Prior to the commencement of the approved use landscaping shall be in place that is in accordance with a landscape scheme that has previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall a) be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's Landscape Guidelines (Maidstone Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012). b) show all existing trees, hedges and blocks of landscaping on, and immediately adjacent to, the site and indicate whether they are to be retained or removed, c) provide details of additional native planting along to the West of the proposed parking area. d) provide a planting schedule (including location, planting species and size). e) provide implementation details and a [5] year management plan.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual amenity and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Landscaping completion and replacement within five years
conditions.text:
All landscaping specified in the approved details shall be completed by the end of the first planting season (October to February) following the commencement of the uses hereby approved. Any of the approved landscaping which fails to establish or any trees or plants which, within five years from the first occupation of the property, are removed, die or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their long term amenity value has been adversely affected shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be approved – ILP GN01 and BCT bat guidance compliance

Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the countryside and protected species.

conditions.summary: Parking and turning areas to remain unobstructed

conditions.summary: Use restricted to B2 and E(g) uses only

conditions.summary: Decentralised/renewable or low-carbon energy – minimum 10% of annual energy requirements
conditions.text:
Prior to first commencement of the approved use, a decentralised and renewable or low-carbon sources of energy shall be incorporated into the development to provide at least 10% of total annual energy requirements of the development and measures to improve energy efficiency. The decentralised and renewable or low-carbon sources of energy and measures to improve energy efficiency shall be in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority and once installed the decentralised and renewable or low-carbon sources of energy and measures to improve energy efficiency shall be retained and maintained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure an energy efficient form of development.

conditions.summary: BREEAM 'Very Good' rating post-construction certificate required

Alternatively, prior to the commencement of the approved use, information shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority that satisfactorily demonstrates firstly why the 'Very Good' standard cannot be met and secondly to show that the development achieves the maximum possible level of building sustainability.
Reason: To ensure that the development achieves a high standard of sustainability and makes efficient use of resources.

The scheme shall consist of the enhancement of ecology through integrated methods into the design and appearance of the building by means such as swift bricks, bat tubes or bee bricks, and through the provision within the site curtilage such as bird boxes, bat boxes, bug hotels, log piles, wildflower planting and hedgehog corridors. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation of the buildings and all features shall be retained and maintained thereafter.

conditions.summary: BREEAM Very Good rating to be achieved and certified within 6 months of first use

A final certificate shall be issued to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing within 6 months of the first use of the building(s) to certify that at a Very Good BREEAM UK New Construction Version 6.1 rating has been achieved.
Reason: To ensure that the development achieves a high standard of sustainability and makes efficient use of resources.

conditions.summary: Contamination encountered during works to be assessed, remediated and closure report submitted
conditions.text:
If during demolition or construction works evidence of potential contamination is encountered, works shall cease and the site fully assessed to enable an appropriate remediation plan to be developed. Works shall not re-commence until an appropriate remediation scheme has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority and the remediation has been completed. Notwithstanding the above paragraph and in any event, upon completion of the building works, this condition shall not be discharged until a closure report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The closure report shall include details of (a) Details of any sampling and remediation works conducted and quality assurance certificates to show that the works have been carried out in full in accordance with the approved methodology. (b) Details of any post-remedial sampling and analysis to show the site has reached the required clean-up criteria shall be included in the closure report together with the necessary documentation detailing what waste materials have been removed from the site. (c) If no contamination has been discovered during the build then evidence (e.g. photos or letters from site manager) to show that no contamination was discovered should be included.
Reason: In the interests of protecting the health of future occupants from any below ground pollutants.

conditions.summary: Construction hours restricted to Mon–Fri 0800–1800, Sat 0800–1300, no Sundays or Bank Holidays
conditions.text:

Reason: In the interest of the amenities of occupies of neighbouring properties.

conditions.summary: Oil/fuel/chemical storage on impervious bunded bases with 110% bund capacity
conditions.text:
Any facilities used for the storage of oils, fuels or chemicals shall be sited on impervious bases and surrounded by impervious bund walls. The bund capacity shall give 110% of the total volume of the tanks.
Reason: In the interests of neighbouring amenity.

conditions.summary: Operational plant noise limit – rating level ≥5dB below LA90 background (BS 4142:2014)

In exceptional circumstances, such as areas with a very low background or where assessment penalties total above 5 the applicant's consultant should contact the Council's Environmental Protection Team (ehadmin@midkent.gov.uk) to agree a site specific target level. Any mitigation measures approved through this condition shall be implemented prior to first use of the plant and equipment and retained and maintained at all times thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of aural amenity.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain – Biodiversity Gain Plan required before development begins
conditions.text: Paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 states that planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the "biodiversity gain condition" which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply.

conditions.summary: Failure to demonstrate 10% Biodiversity Net Gain
conditions.text: The application has failed to demonstrate that the necessary 10% Biodiversity Net Gain can be achieved, and as such there is no evidence that a biodiversity gain condition is capable of being successfully discharged. The net loss of biodiversity would have an adverse impact on the character and appearance of the area and as such would be contrary to National Planning Policy Guidance, paragraph: 019, policies LPRSP9, LPRSP14A, LPRSP15, LPRINF3 and LPRQD4 of the Maidstone Borough Council Local Plan Review (2021-2038), as well as Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as inserted by Schedule 14 of the Environment Act 2021).

conditions.summary: Failure to demonstrate flood resistance and resilience for battery unit and solar panels
conditions.text: The application has failed to demonstrate that the development is or can be reasonably made appropriately flood resistant and resilient and that the proposed battery unit and/or the proposed solar panels could remain operational during a flood event. The proposal is therefore contrary to paragraph 173 of the NPPF, and policies LPRSP9, LPRSP14A, LPRSP15, LPRINF3 and LPRQD4 of the Maidstone Borough Council Local Plan Review (2021-2038).

The application therefore fails to comply with Schedule 2 Part A of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (the UCO) as amended by the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2020. A Lawful Development Certificate cannot be issued.

conditions.summary: Refusal: insufficient evidence of lawful B8 storage use for 10-year period
conditions.text: Submitted information is not sufficiently precise or unambiguous to determine on the balance of probabilities that the existing building has been used as a storage building under Use Class B8 of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) for the 10 years preceding the application submission. Evidence indicates that there have been substantial breaks in the use of the site over the previous 10 years. During these breaks no breach appeared to be taking place and enforcement action could not have reasonably been taken at these times. As such, these periods do not contribute towards the rolling period of years that would otherwise contribute to immunity. For these reasons, this application for a Lawful Development Certificate (existing) is refused.

conditions.summary: Approved landscaping to be in place by end of first planting season
conditions.text: The approved landscaping associated with the individual dwellings shall be in place at the end of the first planting and seeding season following completion of the relevant individual dwelling. Any other communal, shared or street landscaping shall be in place at the end of the first planting and seeding season following completion of the final unit. Any trees or plants, which, within a period of 5 years from the completion of the development die, are removed, or become seriously damaged or diseased, shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species. Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development, and in the interests of residential amenity and biodiversity enhancement.

conditions.summary: Ecology enhancement measures in place prior to first occupation
conditions.text: Prior to first occupation of the relevant property, the associated ecology enhancement measures shown on the approved plans shall be in place, with the measures therefter retained for the lifetime of the development. Reason: To protect and enhance the ecology on the site in the future.

conditions.summary: Tree protection details in accordance with BS 5837 to be submitted
conditions.text: No further work shall take place until details of protection for trees and new areas of structural planting in accordance with the current edition of BS 5837 have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. All trees to be retained must be protected by barriers and/or ground protection. Nothing shall be stored or placed, nor fires lit, within any of the protected areas. No alterations shall be made to the siting of barriers and/or ground protection, nor ground levels changed, nor excavations made within these areas without the written consent of the local planning authority. These measures shall be maintained until all equipment, machinery and surplus materials have been removed from the site. Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Retention of cut timber for saproxylic organism colonisation
conditions.text: All cut timber/wood between 15cm and 60cm in diameter, together with any senescent and rotting wood, should be retained and stacked safely on site for the colonisation of saproxylic organisms, except where an alternative proposal has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Reason: In the interests of wildlife and biodiversity.

conditions.summary: Minimum one electric vehicle charging point per dwelling prior to occupation
conditions.text: Each individual dwelling hereby approved shall not be occupied until a minimum of one electric vehicle charging point has been installed on its associated carport/wagon shed, and shall thereafter be retained for that purpose. Reason: To promote the reduction of CO2 emissions through the use of low emissions vehicles.

conditions.summary: Programme of building recording to be agreed and implemented
conditions.text: No further work shall take place until the applicant, or their agents or successors in title, have secured the implementation of a programme of building recording in accordance with a written specification and timetable which has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All works shall proceed in accordance with the approved measures. Reason: To ensure that historic building features are properly examined and recorded.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan to be submitted and approved
conditions.text: No further works shall take place until a Construction Management Plan for the site has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Construction Management Plan shall include the following details- (a) Routing of construction and delivery vehicles to / from site (b) Parking and turning areas for construction and delivery vehicles and site personnel (c) Timing of deliveries (d) Provision of wheel washing facilities (e) Temporary traffic management / signage (f) Measures to control dust and potential use of asbestos in the existing building. The construction works shall proceed only in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan. Reason: In the interests of residential amenity and highway safety.

Only non-plastic guards shall be used for new trees and hedgerows, and no Sycamore trees shall be planted.

conditions.summary: Approved landscaping to be carried out in first planting season and retained for 10 years

The approved landscaping shall be retained for at least 10 years following its implementation and shall be managed and retained strictly in accordance with the approved specification/management plan, and any approved or retained seeding or turfing which fails to establish or any trees or plants which, before a period of 10 years from the completion of the development has expired, die or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their amenity value has been adversely affected, shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.

conditions.summary: Ecology enhancements details to be submitted and approved prior to first occupation

These details shall include identifying the location and height, and the make/specification of the enhancements; and the development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, with all features being maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of securing ecology enhancements.

conditions.summary: Secured by Design details to be submitted and approved prior to first occupation

The approved details shall be in place prior to the first occupation of the of the development hereby approved and shall be maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of promoting safe and secure communities and environment.

conditions.summary: No external lighting without prior approval; details to accord with ILP guidance
conditions.text:
No external lighting, whether temporary or permanent, shall be placed or erected on the site unless details are first submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Submitted details shall: (a) be in accordance with the Institute of Lighting Engineers Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Lighting, 01/21 - The Reduction Of Obtrusive Light (and any subsequent revisions); (b) include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill; (c) only include external lighting that is both low level and on motion sensors. The external lighting shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the first use of the lighting.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

Reason: In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: 16 parking spaces and vehicle turning areas to be available prior to first use

No development, whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any order revoking and re-enacting that Order, with or without modification) or not, shall be carried out on the areas indicated or in such a position as to preclude vehicular access to them.
Reason: Development without adequate parking/turning provision is likely to lead to parking inconvenience to other road users.

Reason: To ensure an energy efficient form of development.

conditions.summary: Ecological enhancement scheme (bird/bat boxes, wildflower planting etc.) pre-operation
conditions.text:
Prior to operation of the solar panels hereby approved, details of a scheme for the enhancement of ecology on the site shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall consist of the enhancement of ecology through the provision on site of bird boxes, bat boxes, bug hotels, log piles, wildflower planting and hedgehog corridors. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and all features shall be maintained thereafter.
Reason: To enhance the ecology on the site in the future.

conditions.summary: Landscaping scheme to be submitted and approved prior to first operation
conditions.text:
Prior to first operation of the solar panels hereby approved landscaping shall be in place that is in accordance with a landscape scheme that has previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall a) be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's Landscape Guidelines (Maidstone Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012). b) show all existing trees, hedges and blocks of landscaping on, and immediately adjacent to, the site and indicate whether they are to be retained or removed, c) provide details of additional native planting surrounding the solar panels as shown in drawing no. 24_03_P03 D. d) provide a planting schedule (including location, planting species and size). e) provide implementation details and a [5] year management plan.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual amenity and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Landscaping completion by end of first planting season and 5-year replacement obligation
conditions.text:
All landscaping specified in the approved details shall be completed by the end of the first planting season (October to February) following first use of the solar panels hereby approved. Any of the approved landscaping which fails to establish or any trees or plants which, within five years from the first planting, are removed, die or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their long term amenity value has been adversely affected shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be approved in writing prior to installation
conditions.text:
Any external lighting installed on the site (whether permanent or temporary) shall be in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. a) be in accordance with the Institute of Lighting Professionals Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Light, GN01, dated 2011 (and any subsequent revisions) b) follow the recommendations within the Bat Conservation Trust's 'Guidance Note 8 Bats and Artificial Lighting'. c) include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the subsequently approved details and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the countryside and protected species.

conditions.summary: Removal of solar panels and restoration of land within 6 months of ceasing operation
conditions.text:
Within 6 months of the solar panels ceasing to be operational, they and all associated infrastructure shall be removed, and the land restored to its previous condition.
Reason: To ensure the long-term appearance and use of the land is preserved after the use ceases.

conditions.summary: Acoustic report (including low frequency noise) to be approved prior to first operation
conditions.text:
Prior to first operation of the solar panels hereby approved, an acoustic report assessing noise impact shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall address the issue of noise (including low frequency noise) and vibration from the facility to ensure that there is no loss of amenity to residential or commercial properties. For residential accommodation, the scheme shall ensure that the low frequency noise emitted from the equipment is controlled so that it does not exceed the Low Frequency Criterion Curve for the 10 to 160Hz third octave bands inside residential accommodation as described in The DEFRA Procedure for the assessment of low frequency noise complaints 2011 (NANR45). The equipment shall be maintained in a condition so that it complies with the levels and mitigation measures specified in the approved acoustic report, whenever it is operating. After installation of the approved plant no new plant shall be used without the written consent of the local planning authority.
Reason: In the interest of upholding high standards of neighbour amenity.

conditions.summary: Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) for 10% BNG over 30 years
conditions.text:
No development shall take place until a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The HMMP shall: (a) show a minimum of 10% onsite biodiversity net gain (submitted and approved through the Biodiversity Gain Plan) maintained for a period of 30 years from completion of the development; (b) include a non-technical summary; (c) include the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the HMMP; (d) include the planned habitat creation and enhancement works; (e) include the management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for a period of 30 years; and (f) include the monitoring methodology with monitoring reports submitted on year 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 30. Written notice shall be submitted to the local planning authority when habitat creation and enhancement works as set out in the HMMP have been completed.

conditions.text:
Prior to first operation of the solar panels hereby approved a landscape scheme shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall: a) be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's landscape character guidance (Maidstone Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012). b) include details of the number, size, species, maturity, spacing and position of retained and proposed native trees and landscaping and c) include a ten [10] year landscape management plan for the retained and proposed native trees and landscaping (Only non-plastic guards shall be used for the new trees and hedgerows). conditions.text:

Any of the approved landscaping which fails to establish or any trees or plants which, within five years from the first planting, are removed, die or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their long term amenity value has been adversely affected shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.

The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the subsequently approved details and retained and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the countryside and protected species.

Reason: In the interests of protecting residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) for 10% BNG over 30 years

The HMMP shall: a. show a minimum of 10% onsite biodiversity net gain maintained for a period of 30 years from completion of the development; b. include a non-technical summary; c. include the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the HMMP; d. include the planned habitat creation and enhancement works; e. include the management measures to maintain habitat for 30 years; and f. include the monitoring methodology with monitoring reports submitted on year 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 30. The development shall be implemented in full accordance with the approved HMMP. Written notice shall be submitted to the local planning authority when habitat creation and enhancement works have been completed.
Reason: To ensure measurable net gains to biodiversity.

conditions.summary: Refusal reason – harm to countryside, landscape and Kent Downs National Landscape
conditions.text: The proposed development would cause significant harm to the character and appearance of the countryside and landscape within the local area through its scale (extent of area covered), urban appearance, and prominence from public vantage points. It would also have a significant harmful impact on the Kent Downs National Landscape and therefore fail to conserve or enhance this National Landscape. This would be contrary to policies LPRSP9 (Parts 2 and 4) and LPRQD4 (Parts 1 and 2) of the Maidstone Local Plan Review, principles SD2, SD3, and SD5 of the Kent Downs AONB Management Plan, paragraphs 187(a) and (b) and 189 of the NPPF. The development would also fail to further the purpose of conserving or enhancing the natural beauty of the National Landscape as required under Section 245 of the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023. The 40 year lifespan or benefits of the development are not considered to outweigh this conflict with the Development Plan or national policy.

conditions.summary: Refusal reason – exceptional circumstances for major development in National Landscape not demonstrated
conditions.text: Although the need for, and level of, renewable energy generation from the development is considered to be in the public interest, the development would have a minimal impact upon the local economy, the scope for developing outside the National Landscape has not been demonstrated as being unfeasible, it would have a harmful impact on the recreational enjoyment opportunity experienced on the North Downs Way National Trail, and it would cause significant harm to the Kent Downs National Landscape. It is therefore considered that exceptional circumstances have not been demonstrated to allow major development in the National Landscape contrary to paragraph 190 of the NPPF.

The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the subsequently approved details and retained and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the countryside and protected species

conditions.summary: All construction and tree protection to comply with approved Arboricultural Assessment and BS 5837
conditions.text:
All construction activities and tree protection shall be carried out in accordance with the approved pre-development Arboricultural Assessment Report Rev A prepared by Sylvanarb, dated 26.06.2025 and file reference SA/2351/25-A, Tree Protection Plan prepared by Sylvanarb 16.06.2025, reference FST/TPP/2328-03-A. The development hereby approved shall not commence until tree protection is in place in accordance with the current edition of BS 5837. All trees to be retained must be protected by barriers and/or ground protection. No equipment, plant, machinery or materials shall be brought onto the site prior to the erection of approved barriers and/or ground protection except to carry out pre commencement operations approved in writing by the local planning authority. Nothing shall be stored or placed, nor fires lit, within any of the protected areas.
Reason: in the interests of landscape, visual impact and amenity of the area, and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development

conditions.summary: Acoustic assessment for renewable energy plant prior to installation (BS 4142)
conditions.text:
Prior to installation of the renewable equipment (previously approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority through condition 7.) an acoustic assessment and subsequent report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The acoustic assessment and report shall be completed by a suitably qualified and competent person to demonstrate that the rating level of noise emitted from any plant and equipment to be installed on the site (determined using the guidance of the current version of BS 4142 for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) is 5dB below the existing measured background noise level LA90, T. Where the background sound level is below 30dB(A) or where assessment penalties total above 5dB the applicant's consultant shall contact the Environmental Protection Team to agree a site-specific target level.
Reason: In the interest of safeguarding existing amenity of adjacent occupiers.

conditions.summary: Pre-commencement archaeological field evaluation, investigation and post-excavation reporting
conditions.text:
Prior to the commencement of development, the applicant, or their agents or successors in title, will secure: i) archaeological field evaluation works in accordance with a specification and written timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority; and ii) further archaeological investigation, recording and reporting, determined by the results of the evaluation, in accordance with a specification and timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority; iii) programme of post excavation assessment and publication. The development shall only proceed in accordance with the agreed archaeological details.
Reason: To ensure that features of archaeological interest are properly examined, recorded, reported and disseminated.

conditions.summary: Pre-commencement sustainable surface water drainage scheme including SuDS and climate change
conditions.text:
Prior to the commencement of development, a detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme for the site shall be submitted to (and approved in writing by) the local planning authority. The submitted scheme shall demonstrate compliance with the required technical standards at the time of submission and shall demonstrate that the surface water generated by this development (for all rainfall durations and intensities up to and including the climate change adjusted critical 100 year storm) can be accommodated and disposed of within the curtilage of the site without increase to flood risk on or offsite. The drainage scheme shall also demonstrate: i) that silt and pollutants resulting from the site use can be adequately managed to ensure there is no pollution risk to receiving waters. ii) appropriate operational, maintenance and access requirements for each drainage feature or SuDS component are adequately considered.
Reason: To ensure the development is served by satisfactory arrangements for the disposal of surface water and to ensure that the development does not exacerbate the risk of on/off site flooding.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage verification report prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of the development a Verification Report, pertaining to the surface water drainage system and prepared by a suitably competent person, shall have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The Report shall demonstrate that the drainage system constructed is consistent with that which was approved. The Report shall contain information and evidence (including photographs) of details and locations of inlets, outlets and control structures; landscape plans; full as built drawings; information pertinent to the installation of those items identified on the critical drainage assets drawing; and, the submission of an operation and maintenance manual for the sustainable drainage scheme as constructed.
Reason: To ensure that flood risks from development to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those risks to controlled waters, property and ecological systems.

conditions.summary: Parking and turning areas to be kept free from obstruction at all times
conditions.text:
No development, whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any order revoking and re-enacting that Order, with or without modification) or not, shall be carried out on the parking and turning areas indicated on the approved plans or in such a position as to preclude vehicular access to them.
Reason: Development without adequate parking/turning provision is likely to lead to parking inconvenient to other road users and in the interests of road safety.

conditions.summary: Buildings to achieve BREEAM Very Good rating (UK New Construction Version 6.1)
conditions.text:
The buildings hereby approved shall achieve a Very Good BREEAM UK New Construction Version 6.1 rating including maximising energy and water efficiencies under the mandatory energy and water credits. A final certificate shall be issued to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing within 6 months of the first occupation of the relevant building to certify that at a Very Good BREEAM UK New Construction Version 6.1 rating has been achieved.
Reason: To ensure a sustainable form of development

conditions.summary: Community use agreement for wider public access to facilities outside school hours
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of the development, a community use agreement shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority. The community use agreement shall set out measures to secure access to the facilities by the wider community outside the normal school day. The facilities shall thereafter be made available in accordance with the approved agreement.
Reason: To ensure dual use of facilities for new schools for recreation, in accordance with policy LPRINF2 and the NPPF.

conditions.summary: Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) for minimum 10% BNG over 30 years
conditions.text:
No development shall take place until a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The HMMP shall show how the minimum 10% onsite biodiversity net gain (submitted and approved through the Biodiversity Gain Plan) for a period of 30 years from completion of the development will be maintained and the HMMP shall include: (i) a non-technical summary; (ii) the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the HMMP; (iii) the planned habitat creation and enhancement works; (iv) the management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for a period of 30 years from the completion of development; and (v) the monitoring methodology and frequency.
Reason: To ensure measurable net gains to biodiversity.

conditions.summary: Acoustic assessment, noise attenuation scheme and implementation timetable (BS4142)
conditions.text:
The use hereby approved shall cease and all associated material shall be removed within 28 days of the date of failure to meet any one of the requirements set out in (a) to (d) below:
(a) Within 3 months of the date of this decision a scheme, hereafter referred to as the Site Development Scheme, shall have been submitted for the written approval of the local planning authority. The Site Development Scheme shall include:
(i) An acoustic assessment and subsequent report to demonstrate that the rating level of noise emitted from any plant and equipment on the site (determined using the guidance of the current version of BS 4142 for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) is 5dB below the existing measured background noise level LA90, T. Where the background sound level is below 30dB(A) or where assessment penalties total above 5dB the applicant's consultant shall contact the Environmental Protection Team to agree a site-specific target level.
(ii) Details of attenuation measures to meet the noise levels specified above.
(iii) A timetable for implementation of the agreed attenuation measures in the Site Development Scheme.
(b) If within 11 months of the date of this decision the local planning authority refuse to approve the Site Development Scheme or fail to give a decision within the prescribed period, an appeal shall have been made to, and accepted as validly made by, the Secretary of State.
(c) If an appeal is made in pursuance of above, that appeal shall have been finally determined and submitted Site Development Scheme shall have been approved by Secretary of State.
(d) The approved Site Development Scheme shall have been carried out and completed in accordance with the approved timetable.
Reason: No such details have been submitted and in the interest of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Maintenance of acoustic equipment and attenuation measures
conditions.text:
The equipment and attenuation required by condition 3 shall be maintained in a condition so that it complies with the levels and mitigation measures specified in the approved acoustic report, whenever it is operating. After installation of the approved plant no new plant shall be used without the prior written permission of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: No such details have been submitted and in the interest of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Impervious bunded storage for oils, fuels or chemicals (110% capacity)
conditions.text:
Any facilities used for the storage of oils, fuels or chemicals shall be sited on impervious bases and surrounded by impervious bund walls. The bund capacity shall give 110% of the total volume of the tanks.
Reason: To prevent contamination and in the interest of residential amenity.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain condition – Biodiversity Gain Plan required before development begins
conditions.text: Paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 states that planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the 'biodiversity gain condition' which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply.

The Construction Management Plan shall include the following details: (a) Routing of construction and delivery vehicles to / from site (b) Parking and turning areas for construction and delivery vehicles and site personnel (c) Timing of deliveries (d) Temporary traffic management / signage (e) Measures to control dust. (g) Measures to prevent the discharge of surface water onto the highway. The construction works shall proceed only in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan.
Reason: In the interests of residential amenity and highway safety.

conditions.summary: Restriction on demolition/construction hours
conditions.text:
No demolition/construction activities shall take place, other than between 0800 to 1800 hours (Monday to Friday) and 0800 to 1300 hours (Saturday) with no working activities on Sunday or Bank Holiday.
Reason: In the interest of the amenities of occupiers of neighbouring properties.

conditions.summary: External materials to match Design and Access Statement
conditions.text:
The materials to be used in the development hereby approved shall be as indicated in the Design and Access Statement. The materials shall be permanently retained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: On-site ecology enhancement measures to be in place prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved the on-site ecology enhancement measures shown on drawing BDS-VCH-P08 (Biodiversity Site Plan) (received on 4th July 2024), shall be in place. All features shall be retained and maintained permanently thereafter.
Reason: To enhance ecology and biodiversity on the site.

conditions.summary: Approved landscaping scheme to be in place after first planting season
conditions.text:
Notwithstanding the details submitted in Drawing number: BDS-VCH-P04C (Proposed Site Plan), at the end of the first planting season (October to February) following first occupation of any of the approved apartments landscaping shall be in place, that shall be in accordance with a landscape scheme that has previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The landscaping shall be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's landscape character guidance (Maidstone Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012). The landscaping shall include: a) Details of all existing trees, hedgerows, and blocks of landscaping on, and immediately adjacent to, the site and indicate whether they are to be retained or removed. b) Details of the number, size, species, maturity, spacing and position of proposed trees and landscaping... c) A timetable of implementation of the approved scheme and d) A five [5] year landscape management plan (Only non-plastic guards shall be used for the new trees and hedgerows, and no Sycamore trees shall be planted).
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact, and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Replacement planting for failed landscaping within five years
conditions.text:
Any landscaping which fails to establish or any existing or proposed trees or plants which, within five years from planting are removed, die, or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their long-term amenity value has been adversely affected shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact, and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: External amenity space to be provided prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved external amenity space shall be provided for all the apartments including: a) Direct access from the ground floor units b) Defensible space in front of all ground floor windows and c) Communal space accessible for the occupiers of the apartments at first and second floor levels d) The areas of approved amenity space shall be retained and maintained in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact, and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Management plan for open areas required prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved a management plan, including management responsibilities and maintenance schedules for the open areas of the application site (excluding private amenity space) shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The approved management plan shall be followed thereafter.
Reason: To ensure the appropriate protection of wildlife and design of supporting habitat.

conditions.summary: Bin storage to be in place prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, the bin storage shown on the approved plans shall be in place. These details will be retained and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Waste collection strategy required prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, a waste collection strategy shall be in place that is in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The waste strategy shall set out arrangements for the collection of waste including the collection location and measures to ensure that bins are returned to the bin storage area. These details will be maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Minimum three electric vehicle charging points (Mode 3/SMART) prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, a minimum of three operational electric vehicle charging points for low-emission plug-in vehicles shall be installed on the site and ready for the use by new occupants with the electric vehicle charging points thereafter retained and maintained operational as such for that purpose. The electric vehicle charging points shall be provided to Mode 3 standard (providing up to 7kw) and SMART (enabling Wifi connection).
Reason: To promote sustainable travel choices and the reduction of CO2 emissions through use of low emissions vehicles.

conditions.summary: Decentralised/renewable/low-carbon energy to be incorporated prior to first occupation
conditions.text:
Prior to first occupation of any of the apartments hereby approved, the decentralised and renewable or low-carbon sources of energy shown on drawing number: BDS-VCH-P09 (Sustainability Plan) shall be incorporated into the development hereby approved. The decentralised and renewable or low-carbon sources of energy shall be maintained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure an energy efficient form of development.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme to be approved in writing; bat conservation trust guidelines to apply
conditions.text:
Any external lighting installed on the site (whether permanent or temporary) shall be in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. The approved details shall be in accordance with bat conservation trust guidelines and the Institute of Lighting Obtrusive Light Limitations for Exterior Lighting Installations for Environmental Zone E1. The scheme of lighting shall be installed, maintained and operated thereafter in accordance with the approved scheme.
Reason: In order to prevent undue light pollution and to protect wildlife.

conditions.summary: Internal/external noise levels to comply with BS 8233:2014 prior to window installation

The work specified in the approved scheme shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation of the any of the relevant apartments hereby approved and retained and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of amenity.

conditions.summary: Water efficiency standard of 110 litres per person per day (Building Regs Part G2)

Reason: To ensure a sustainable form of development.

No apartment shall be occupied until all the works necessary have been implemented in accordance with the approved details. a) Provide information about the design storm period and intensity, the method employed to delay and control the surface water discharged from the site, including any requirement for the provision of a balancing pond and the measures taken to prevent pollution of the receiving groundwater and/or surface waters. b) Provide permeable surfacing for the parking area, including a scheme of maintenance. c) Include a timetable for its implementation in relation to the development; and, d) Provide a management and maintenance plan for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In the interests of pollution and flood prevention.

conditions.summary: Landscaping scheme to be submitted, approved and implemented post-occupation
conditions.text:
At the end of the first planting season (October to February) following first occupation of the approved accommodation landscaping shall be in place that is in accordance with a landscape scheme that has previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The landscape scheme shall be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's landscape character guidance. The scheme shall show all existing landscaping on, and immediately adjacent to, the site and, provide details of additional on-site planting to mitigate loss of amenity and biodiversity value and include a planting specification, implementation details and a [5] year management plan. Any trees or plants, which, within a period of 5 years from the completion of the development die, are removed, or become seriously damaged or diseased, shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species.
Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual amenity and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Construction hours restricted (Mon–Fri 0800–1800, Sat 0800–1300, no Sundays/Bank Holidays)
conditions.text:

Reason: In the interest of the amenities of occupies of neighbouring properties.

conditions.summary: Construction Method Statement to be submitted and approved prior to development
conditions.text:
No development shall take place, until a Construction Method Statement has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The approved Statement shall be adhered to throughout the construction period. The Statement shall provide for:
i. the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors
ii. loading and unloading of plant and materials
i. storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development
iv. the erection and maintenance of security hoarding
v. wheel washing facilities
vi. a scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works
Reason: In the interests of the amenities of the area and highway safety and convenience.

Reason: In the interests of landscape, visual impact, and amenity of the area and to ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development.

conditions.summary: Statutory Biodiversity Net Gain condition – Biodiversity Gain Plan required
conditions.text: Paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 states that planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the "biodiversity gain condition" which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply.

conditions.summary: Unjustified loss of community facility and visitor accommodation (pub/hotel viability)
conditions.text: The application has failed to demonstrate that the existing public house and hotel are not viable, that there is no demand for their use, or that alternative community facilities or those designated as 'Principal Tourism Assets' could not operate from the site. The proposed development would therefore result in the unjustified loss of a community facility and visitor accommodation, contrary to policies CP1(9) and CP6 of the Swale Borough Local Plan 2017 and the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Inadequate off-street parking provision – highway safety
conditions.text: The proposal, by virtue of failing to provide adequate off-street vehicle parking in accordance with the Swale Borough Council Parking Standards SPD, would lead to an increase in on-street parking demand in a location where there is limited capacity to safely accommodate such additional pressure. This shortfall would likely result in indiscriminate or hazardous parking on the public highway, to the detriment of highway safety and the free flow of traffic. As such, the proposal is contrary to policies DM7 and Policy CP2 of the Swale Borough Local Plan 2017 and NPPF.

conditions.summary: Inadequate living conditions for future occupiers – noise and disturbance
conditions.text: The proposed development would fail to provide adequate living conditions for future occupiers with regards to noise and disturbance in conflict with policy DM14 of the Swale Borough Local Plan 2017 and the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Failure to demonstrate sequential flood risk test satisfied
conditions.text: The applicant has failed to demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority that there are no reasonably available sites appropriate for the development hereby proposed in areas of lower probability of flooding. As such, the proposed development is contrary to policies DM21 of the Swale Borough Local Plan 2017 along with paragraphs 170 and 174 the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Recreational disturbance to Swale SPA – no SAMMS contribution secured
conditions.text: The proposed development will create potential for recreational disturbance to the Swale Special Protection Area. The application submission does not include an appropriate financial contribution to the Thames, Medway and Swale Strategic Access Management and Monitoring Strategy (SAMMS), or the means of securing such a contribution, and therefore fails to provide adequate mitigation against that potential harm. The development would therefore affect the integrity of this designated European site and would be contrary to the aims of policies ST1, DM14, and DM28 of the adopted Swale Borough Local Plan 2017 and the NPPF.
